notes/lepton_work.md:1500:That assumption is no longer vague. It is precisely the autonomous self-reproducing eigenmode closure of the isolated support channel, together with the central-sign closure on the mixed subbundle. If those two pieces can be derived rather than imposed, the session’s half-integer lock becomes a true theorem of the model. If not, the route remains an elegant but conditional possibility.
notes/lepton_work.md:1504:### 17.1 Derive autonomous eigenmode closure from the actual support/leakage dynamics
notes/lepton_work.md:1506:The next session should not reopen the whole lepton audit from scratch. It should start from the end-state reached here and ask one sharply framed question:
notes/lepton_work.md:1510:\text{Can the actual support/leakage dynamics of an isolated particle derive the autonomous eigenmode closure?}
notes/lepton_work.md:1514:In the language of the one-cycle amplitude map, that means testing whether the isolated particle’s support channel is genuinely a self-reproducing trapped eigenmode
notes/lepton_work.md:1518:rather than merely a pump-balanced or leakage-balanced steady state. The exact ledgers already singled out by the session — through-flow, back-pressure, scalar leakage, and mixed work — are the right place to do this, because they are the only file-grounded scalar channels that can feed the common phase sector. So the highest-leverage next move is not “derive more spin structure,” but “derive the closure that kills (\phi_0).”
notes/lepton_work.md:1534:That would upgrade the present closure from a conditional theorem to the first really file-grounded same-charge half-flux theorem in the program.
notes/lepton_work.md:1536:### 17.3 What failure would mean for the minimal charged-lepton program
notes/lepton_work.md:1542:with no rigid half-integer lock. In that case the minimal charged-lepton route would still have an interesting mixed-sector rotor and possibly an induced (P_{22}) doublet mechanism, but it would still lack a file-grounded same-charge spinor quantizer. At that point the program would either have to find a new non-Abelian mixed transport law or accept that the present ontology cannot yet finish the charged-lepton target. This is exactly the sort of falsification-first endpoint the handoff methodology asked for from the beginning.

     1	# Branch-Realization Test — Problem Brief
     2	
     3	**For:** a computational physicist, or an AI system capable of validated numerical PDE work.
     4	**From:** Trevor Norris (independent researcher).
     5	**Status of the work being tested:** a speculative research program. This brief asks for a *decisive numerical test*, not an endorsement of the underlying model.
     6	
     7	---
     8	
     9	## 1. What I'm asking for, in one paragraph
    10	
    11	I have a parent field theory and a set of reduced target observables that the theory is *supposed* to reproduce. I need someone to numerically realize the relevant branch of the parent PDE and determine — **target-blind, with a proper error budget** — whether the realized branch returns those targets, or whether the apparent agreement is numerical artifact. A trustworthy *no* is as valuable to me as a trustworthy *yes*. What I cannot use is another run that produces numbers without establishing that the numbers are scientifically valid.
    12	
    13	---
    14	
    15	## 2. The system (decoupled from interpretation)
    16	
    17	You do **not** need to assess the physical interpretation of the model to do this work. Treat it as a well-defined PDE plus a list of observables plus a validation requirement.
    18	
    19	- **Parent system:** a (4+1)D gauged nonlinear Schrödinger / Gross–Pitaevskii field coupled to a localized Maxwell sector, with a stiff polytropic equation of state (exponent n = 5), plus a moving-throat geometry sector.
    20	- **Exact action, gauge handling, boundary protocol, and the throat-field promotion** are specified in the source ledger (see §7). Use those definitions verbatim; do not reconstruct them.
    21	- **The relevant object** is the moving-throat branch: solve it, then extract the reduced impedance / Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) data and the grouped-coefficient observables from the solution.
    22	
    23	---
    24	
    25	## 3. The task
    26	
    27	1. **Realize the branch.** Numerically solve the appropriate stationary (and, where specified, dynamic) moving-throat branch of the parent PDE.
    28	2. **Extract the reduced observables** as defined in the source ledger — at minimum the coefficient bundle (`D0, D2, D4, N0, N2, N4, P0, P2, P4`), the outgoing-normalization scalar `χ_Q`, the prefactor slope `Ξ1 = P1/P0`, the rigid-mouth orbit-lock chart `(U, V)`, and the selected support-placement coordinate. Pull exact definitions from §13.2 and §12 of the source ledger.
    29	3. **Keep the extraction target-blind.** This is the single most important constraint. The target values (§4) must **not** be inserted into the solve, used to tune any free parameter, used to choose a branch, or used to set a stopping criterion. Solve first, extract second, compare to targets **last**.
    30	4. **Pre-register the branch.** Before running, fix and write down *which* branch, boundary conditions, and closure are being realized, and record that choice. The program admits many branches and relaxed/open-system companions; if a miss is allowed to send you to the next branch in search of a pass, the test stops being a falsification and becomes an unbounded search that no negative result can ever end. Name the branch first, then let the result stand.
    31	
    32	---
    33	
    34	## 4. The targets (used only for comparison, after extraction)
    35	
    36	From the source ledger's target card (§13.3 / §13.4). Check the realized branch against these; do not steer toward them.
    37	
    38	- `R_pole = D0(B4+Z4) − 3(M+B2+Z2)^2 = 0`
    39	- `R_norm = m̂0² · S_port · N0/D0 − 54 G c_s^5 / (5 a^5 c^5) = 0`
    40	- `P2 = P4 = 0`
    41	- `R_tail = Θ_tail (c/c_s)^3 − 1 = 0` (if the tail sector is active)
    42	- `χ_Q = 1`, and the 5PN actual-branch conditions `d ln R_tr = d ln R_target = d ln ε_η = 0`
    43	
    44	Take the exact, current form of each from the ledger, not from this summary.
    45	
    46	---
    47	
    48	## 5. Validation requirements (non-negotiable — this is where the prior attempt failed)
    49	
    50	The previous attempt produced a stable, open branch but the data was noise-dominated and could not be certified as scientifically valid. The following are mandatory, and a result without them does not count as an answer.
    51	
    52	1. **Validate before trusting.** Demonstrate the solver on at least one limit with a known analytic or well-benchmarked answer (e.g. a free/linear limit, a known GPE vortex or soliton solution, or a standard GPE benchmark) *before* extracting any unknown observable.
    53	2. **Convergence study.** Refine spatial grid and timestep; show each extracted observable converges and report the observed order of convergence. An observable that drifts under refinement is not a measurement.
    54	3. **Boundary control.** Use absorbing / PML / sponge boundary layers; demonstrate quantitatively that boundary reflections sit below the target signal.
    55	4. **Conservation diagnostics.** Report mass / charge / energy drift (as appropriate to the sector) over the run.
    56	5. **Error budget and noise floor.** State the numerical noise floor explicitly. Every extracted observable must carry a quantitative uncertainty. A match or mismatch with a target is only meaningful relative to that floor.
    57	
    58	---
    59	
    60	## 6. Deliverables and acceptance criteria
    61	
    62	**Deliverables**
    63	1. The validated solver and a reproducible configuration.
    64	2. A validation + convergence report establishing the solver is trustworthy *before* any physics claim.
    65	3. Target-blind extracted values for each observable in §3.2, each with a stated uncertainty.
    66	4. A per-target verdict: does the realized branch meet each target within validated error, and if not, by how much relative to the noise floor?
    67	
    68	**What counts as an answer**
    69	- **Trustworthy NO** — the branch misses one or more targets beyond validated error, or the apparent signal is shown to be numerical artifact. *This is a valid, valuable result.*
    70	- **Trustworthy YES** — the branch returns at least one target, target-blind, within validated error.
    71	- **Not an answer** — numbers produced without the §5 validation report. (The whole point of the exercise is to avoid exactly this.)
    72	
    73	---
    74	
    75	## 7. Interpreting the result (what a pass and a fail actually mean)
    76	
    77	So that the outcome is read correctly by whoever runs this:
    78	
    79	- **A validated, target-blind pass** on one or more targets means the unfitted dynamics reproduce that piece of known physics in a way that could not have been rigged. That is strong evidence the model is a **viable candidate** — it is *consistent with* reality without having been told the answer. It is **not** proof the model is the correct description of reality, because reproducing known physics is non-unique: more than one theory reproduces 1PN gravity, and inverse-square attraction follows from almost any sink model. A pass earns the model a seat among viable candidates; it does not single it out as true.
    80	- **A validated miss, on a pre-registered branch (§3.4)**, falsifies that branch's claim. If the branch was the program's committed prediction, that is a clean negative on the program's core premise.
    81	- **Numbers without the §5 validation report** settle nothing either way.
    82	
    83	The step that would move the model from "viable candidate" to "true claim about the world" is **not** another reproduced target — it is a *novel, confirmed prediction* that diverges from GR/QED and turns out right. That is the purpose of Stage 2.
    84	
    85	---
    86	
    87	## 8. Stage 2 — divergence extraction (conditional; only after a Stage-1 pass)
    88	
    89	Run this only if Stage 1 produced at least one validated target-blind pass. A novel prediction from a branch that cannot reproduce known physics is worthless, so this stage is gated on Stage 1.
    90	
    91	1. **Use the same branch, nothing re-tuned.** All divergence predictions must come from the identical validated, unfitted branch realized in Stage 1. Any new free parameter introduced here voids the result.
    92	2. **Find where the model diverges from GR/QED.** Identify regimes or observables where the model's prediction differs from the incumbent theory, and compute the size of that difference from the branch.
    93	3. **Classify every divergence by testability, honestly:**
    94	   - *Measurable now* — the divergence exceeds current or near-future experimental sensitivity in a regime where data exists or is obtainable. **These are the only ones that matter.** Prioritize them.
    95	   - *Real but below the noise floor* — the divergence is smaller than the §5 numerical noise floor. Not a prediction yet; report as such.
    96	   - *Unmeasurable in principle* — the divergence lives only where no experiment can reach. This is a promissory note, not a test, and must be labeled that way rather than presented as a prediction.
    97	4. **Validate the difference to the same standard.** A claimed divergence must clear the same convergence and error-budget bar as the Stage-1 targets. A "prediction" buried in numerical noise is not a prediction.
    98	
    99	The deliverable of Stage 2 is a short list of *measurable-now* divergences with magnitudes and the specific measurement that would see them — or an honest statement that the model diverges from GR/QED only in regimes nothing can currently probe.
   100	
   101	---

   106	- §1.4 — strict parent action and throat-field promotion status

Settling that question — either way — is the deliverable.

    10	
    11	## 1. What this plan does and does not cover
    12	
    13	This plan is the engineering-side companion to the scientific brief. The brief (see §0 above) specifies *what* must be solved and *what* must be reported. This plan specifies *how*: the discretization shape, the hardware tier, the validation sequence, and the relationship to other parts of the program.
    14	
    15	This plan does **not** alter, override, or weaken the brief. In particular, every §5 validation requirement in the brief is mandatory regardless of what's in this plan, and the pre-registration rule (§3.4 of the brief) is non-negotiable.
    16	
    17	This plan assumes the user's stated project goal (see [[project-analog-framework-goal]] in auto-memory): the deliverable is a working *mathematical analog* between EM and gravity, not an ontology claim. Stage 1 scoring is "the analog operationally works as a bridge," not "evidence the model is true."
    18	
    19	---
    20	
    21	## 2. Computational shape of the problem
    22	
    23	### 2.1 Why the working domain is 2D
    24	
    25	The brief asks for two solves:
    26	
    27	1. **WP1 — Stationary isotropic moving-throat branch** (see `notes/5pn/5pn_stage354_355_computational_handoff.md` §3 and `notes/moving_throat_pde_engine_handoff.md` §9–11).
    28	2. **WP3 — Grouped real P2 weak-axisymmetric tangent** linearized around that branch.
    29	
    30	The parent system is (4+1)D — fields `ψ(X,t)`, `A_M(X,t)`, `R(Ω, w, t)`. Two symmetry facts collapse the working domain to 2D:
    31	
    32	- **Stationary** drops `t`.
    33	- **Isotropic** (spherical symmetry in `(x,y,z)`) drops `Ω`, collapsing the three brane spatial dimensions to a single radial coordinate `r`.
    34	
    35	So on the isotropic branch the fields are functions of `(r, w)` only. The P2 tangent has angular structure fixed by `Y_{2m}`, so it too lives on `(r, w)` as a linear PDE around the WP1 solution.
    36	
    37	This is not an approximation. The 2D mesh **parameterizes 4D field configurations that happen to have spherical symmetry** — the angular content is identically present, just constant along the angular directions because of the symmetry. The same maneuver is what reduces the hydrogen `1s` to a 1D radial ODE, FRW cosmology to a 1D `a(t)` ODE, axisymmetric CFD jets to 2D `(r, z)` meshes, etc. The 4D measure factor `r²` appears explicitly in the discrete operators; the discretization is 3D physics on a 2D mesh, not 2D physics.
    38	
    39	### 2.2 What 2D does and does not capture
    40	
    41	| Captures | Does not capture |
    42	|---|---|
    43	| Full radial and axial flux of fluid through and along the throat | Angular flux (identically zero by symmetry on the isotropic branch) |
    44	| All coefficients `D0, D2, D4, N0, N2, N4, P0, P2, P4` defined on the isotropic branch | Whether the isotropic branch is dynamically stable against general angular perturbations |
    45	| The grouped P2 response operator's low-frequency expansion (`R_pole`, `R_norm`) | Two-throat / multi-body interactions |
    46	| The "induced P_{22} response" mechanism from `notes/lepton_work.md` §10 (it is precisely the linearized P2 tangent) | The full spin-1/2 chain (needs §14 autonomous-eigenmode closure separately) |
    47	| Outgoing DtN data via Robin impedance / PML on the linear tangent | Long-time dynamic radiation propagation |
    48	
    49	The "does not capture" column is intentionally *not* in the brief's scope. Those are downstream tests gated on Stage 1 passing.
    50	
    51	### 2.3 Field count and grid scale
    52	
    53	Unknowns on the `(r, w)` mesh (post-gauge-fixing):
    54	
    55	- `ψ_real, ψ_imag` (or amplitude/phase — Madelung form)
    56	- `A_0, A_r, A_w` (Maxwell components in the axisymmetric reduction)
    57	- `R_0(w)` (throat shape — 1D auxiliary)
    58	- One gauge-fixing scalar or Lagrange multiplier
    59	
    60	Roughly 5–7 coupled fields per cell. Estimated grid scales for Stage 1:
    61	
    62	| Tier | Cells `(N_r × N_w)` | Total DOFs | Hardware | Wall clock per Newton solve |
    63	|---|---|---|---|---|
    64	| Smoke | 512 × 256 | ~0.8M | laptop CPU | minutes |
    65	| Production | 2048 × 1024 | ~12M | A100/A6000 class, 64–128 GB RAM | hours |
    66	| Refined | 8192 × 4096 | ~200M | H100 or dual-A100, 256 GB RAM | ~1 day |
    67	
    68	The §5.2 convergence study needs 3–5 levels; the WP3 tangent on the same mesh is 2–5× cheaper than WP1 because it is linear. Total compute for a complete Stage-1 attempt with validation: **1–4 weeks of intermittent runpods GPU time**, ballpark **$500–$5000** of cloud GPU spend depending on iteration count.
    69	
    70	---
   137	## 5. Relationship to spin-1/2 / lepton_work / autonomous-eigenmode closure
   138	
   139	The brief's framing intersects `notes/lepton_work.md` in a non-obvious way that future sessions need to understand.
   140	
   141	`lepton_work.md` §10 documents that the spin-1/2 mechanism rides on an **induced area-preserving `P_{22}` deformation** of the throat mouth, and §14 documents that the same-charge half-integer quantizer is conditional on the isolated particle being an **autonomous self-reproducing standing-wave GNLS soliton**.
   142	
   143	The relationship to Stage 1:
   144	
   145	- The **stationary isotropic branch** (WP1) **is** the autonomous-eigenmode candidate. A Newton solve that converges to a stationary isotropic configuration with stable support modes is implicitly testing whether the parent PDE admits such an autonomous soliton at all. If WP1 has no solution, the §14 closure is unreachable in this model.
   146	- The **grouped P2 tangent** (WP3) **is** the induced-deformation response. The P_{22} mechanism in `lepton_work.md` §10 is a special case of the broader `Y_{2m}` quadrupole linearized response that the brief tests. The coefficients the brief extracts (`D_2, D_4, N_2, N_4`) characterize the response operator whose poles include the resonance the user described ("bumping a particle causes it to resonate").
   147	- **Stage 1 does not directly test spin-1/2.** That's downstream of `lepton_work.md` §14 + §12 (central-sign holonomy) + the recirculation/plumbing closure. Stage 1 only tests whether the foundational autonomous-eigenmode and P2-response structures exist with the right gravity-side coefficients.
   148	
   149	The user explicitly flagged: *"never assume the simple solution works"* in this system. The brief honors that — its targets are coefficients of the **response operator's low-frequency expansion**, not naïve properties of the static configuration. The feedback structure (inflow pressure ↔ wall energy ↔ standing-wave support ↔ brane closure) is *what determines those coefficients* on the realized branch. A successful Stage 1 means the feedback closes self-consistently and produces the right numbers; a failure tells you which sector of the feedback didn't close.
   150	
   151	---
   152	
   153	## 6. The real failure mode to watch for
   154	
   155	Not in the five prior-project issues. Specific to this problem:
   156	
   157	**Stiff `P = K ρ^5` polytropic conditioning.** The enthalpy `h(ρ) = (5K/4)ρ^4` becomes near-singular as `ρ → 0` inside the throat or near the wall. This makes the Newton Jacobian poorly conditioned (condition number ~ 10⁶ regime, not catastrophic but unfriendly without a good preconditioner). Mitigations:
   158	
   159	- **Geometric or algebraic multigrid** on the linearized operator (this is why the software stack choice matters).
   160	- **Change of variables** — e.g., work in `log ρ` or in a regularized density, so the near-singular region maps to a well-behaved one.
   161	- **Continuation in `K`** — start with a milder EOS, continue to the stiff target value.
   162	
   163	Poorly conditioned Newton solves fail *loudly* (residual stops dropping, GMRES iteration count blows up), which is the opposite of how the prior project's issues manifested. That's a feature: the diagnostic is unambiguous.
   164	
   165	---
   166	
   167	## 7. Sequencing
   168	
   169	Implementation order, with the answer each step gives:
   170	
   171	1. **GPE-soliton or GPE-vortex benchmark on a 2D grid.** Cheap (single-GPU hour or two). Proves discretization + boundary treatment work on a known-analytic problem. *Brief §5.1 requirement.*
   172	2. **Manufactured-solution tests per operator block** (matter, Maxwell, wall). Cheap. Proves discrete operators match continuum operators.
   173	3. **Stationary isotropic branch Newton solve at coarse grid.** Few GPU-hours. End-to-end pipeline smoke test producing a smoke `D0, P0, …` packet.
   174	4. **Convergence study at 3–5 grid levels.** Order-of-day GPU work per level. Establishes noise floor and convergence order for each observable. *Brief §5.2.*
   175	5. **PML / sponge characterization on the tangent.** Demonstrates boundary reflections sit below the target signal. *Brief §5.3.*
   176	6. **Conservation diagnostics.** Mass / charge / energy drift over each run. *Brief §5.4.*
   177	7. **Error budget statement.** Quantitative uncertainty per extracted observable. *Brief §5.5.*
   178	8. **WP3 — P2 tangent on the converged stationary branch.** Day or two. Produces `d ln R_tr, d ln R_target, d ln ε_η`.
   179	9. **Stage-1 verdict.** Compare extracted observables to brief §4 targets within validated error. Honest either way.
   180	
   181	If Stage 1 passes, **Stage 2** (divergence extraction, brief §8) becomes worth running. If it fails trustworthy, the result is publishable and diagnoses *which* sector of the parent theory needs revisiting.

   195	## 9. What success means in the analog-framework frame
   196	
   197	Stage 1 success **is not** "evidence the model describes physical reality." (User has not made and does not intend to make that claim — see [[project-analog-framework-goal]].)
   198	
   199	Stage 1 success **is** "the analog framework is self-consistent and operationally demonstrable: one set of equations, reduced two ways, returning the right coefficients in both reductions, with a validated noise floor." That delivers the project's stated deliverable — a working mathematical bridge between EM and gravity formalisms — at the strongest level a single solo-researcher-plus-AI program can deliver.
   200	
   201	A trustworthy Stage 1 miss is also a valid outcome. It says: the analog as currently written does not close all the way through; here is which coefficient does not match; here is the validated error budget around that statement. That is publishable, citable, and useful — particularly because the prior 4d_1pn_sim attempt could not produce a trustworthy verdict either direction.
   202	
   203	Stage 2 (novel-prediction extraction) is the test of whether the analog also *says something new and right*. Stage 1 is the gate to running Stage 2 honestly.

    19	def stable_hash(obj: Any) -> str:
    20	    payload = json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), default=float).encode("utf-8")
    21	    return hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()

    54	def write_json(path: Path, payload: Any) -> None:
    55	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    56	    path.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

    59	def imported_roots(path: Path) -> Set[str]:
    60	    tree = ast.parse(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), filename=str(path))
    61	    roots: Set[str] = set()
    62	    for node in ast.walk(tree):
    63	        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
    64	            for alias in node.names:
    65	                roots.add(alias.name.split(".", 1)[0])
    66	        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.module:
    67	            roots.add(node.module.split(".", 1)[0] if node.level == 0 else "__future__")
    68	    return roots

    71	def source_import_check() -> Dict[str, Any]:
    72	    issues: List[str] = []
    73	    details: Dict[str, Any] = {}
    74	    for filename, allowed in ALLOWED_IMPORTS.items():
    75	        imports = imported_roots(SIM_DIR / filename)
    76	        banned = sorted(root for root in imports if any(root.startswith(prefix) for prefix in BANNED_IMPORT_PREFIXES))
    77	        unexpected = sorted(imports - allowed)
    78	        details[filename] = {
    79	            "imports": sorted(imports),
    80	            "allowed_imports": sorted(allowed),
    81	            "banned_imports": banned,
    82	            "unexpected_imports": unexpected,
    83	        }
    84	        for root in banned:
    85	            issues.append(f"{filename} imports banned target-evaluation module root {root!r}")
    86	        for root in unexpected:
    87	            issues.append(f"{filename} imports undeclared module root {root!r}")
    88	    return {"name": "source_import_boundary", "pass": not issues, "issues": issues, "details": details}

    91	def status_hash_check(status: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    92	    status_without_hash = dict(status)
    93	    status_without_hash.pop("status_hash", None)
    94	    recomputed = physical_model.stable_hash(status_without_hash)
    95	    stored = status.get("status_hash")
    96	    return {
    97	        "name": "status_hash",
    98	        "pass": stored == recomputed,
    99	        "stored_status_hash": stored,
   100	        "recomputed_status_hash": recomputed,
   101	    }

     1	# Nonlinear Protocol V2
     2	
     3	This is the pre-target protocol for the next simulation layer.  It is not a
     4	target-evaluation script and it should not import V2-21, V2-22A, or V2-22B
     5	target extraction modules.
     6	
     7	## Goal
     8	
     9	Replace the current reduced and manufactured surrogate generators with a real
    10	nonlinear PDE/continuation exporter that writes frozen V2-22B-compatible
    11	packets.  The candidate set, continuation controls, solver tolerances, and
    12	packet freeze hash must be fixed before any target residuals are computed.
    13	
    14	The current ledger does not yet permit that strict physical export.  The
    15	available materials support an effective wall/interface closure and reduced
    16	BdG/Maxwell blocks, but the parent-level `S_eta`/`S_Sigma` promotion and full
    17	coupled physical residual equations are not frozen.  Until that happens,
    18	`verify_physical_model.py` is the executable guard: it records the blocker and
    19	emits no physical branch packets.
    20	
    21	## Unknowns
    22	
    23	The nonlinear solve should at minimum evolve these coupled fields on an open
    24	finite throat:
    25	
    26	- throat radius/support state `R(s)` with `R(0)=R_mouth` and finite open exit
    27	  impedance at `s=L`;
    28	- wall/support profile `chi_eta(s)`;
    29	- BdG support profile(s) `phi_B(s)`;
    30	- mixed port profiles `u(s)` and `w(s)`;
    31	- continuation parameters for geometry, couplings, and exit impedance.
    32	
    33	## Boundary Conditions
    34	
    35	- mouth: Dirichlet anchoring for support profiles and fixed positive
    36	  `R_mouth`;
    37	- exit: open impedance/Robin condition with finite `R_exit > 0`;
    38	- forbidden: hard caps, closed-throat endpoint substitutions, and any
    39	  post-target retuning.
    40	
    41	## Required Pre-Evaluation Checks
    42	
    43	Before target classification, the exporter must pass:
    44	
    45	- manufactured-solution checks for each discretized operator;
    46	- finite-difference or automatic-differentiation Jacobian consistency checks;
    47	- Newton residual and continuation residual thresholds;
    48	- mesh-refinement repeats on at least three grid sizes;
    49	- branch-freeze hash verification;
    50	- negative controls that reject hard-cap, nonpositive-frequency, missing-profile,
    51	  and post-target-mutated packets.
    52	
    53	The current executable readiness layer is:
    54	
    55	- `nonlinear_protocol.py`: machine-readable pre-target protocol and candidate
    56	  freeze-hash helpers;
    57	- `verify_nonlinear_solver.py`: source import boundary, protocol/freeze hashes,
    58	  manufactured nonlinear mesh convergence, analytic-vs-finite-difference
    59	  Jacobian consistency, and continuation sanity.
    60	- `generate_nonlinear_packets.py`: target-blind V2-22B packet exporter for the
    61	  manufactured nonlinear readiness branches.
    62	- `physical_nonlinear_model.py` and `verify_physical_model.py`: executable
    63	  inventory of the strict physical-export blockers and source citations.
    64	
    65	The readiness verifier intentionally emits no V2-22B candidate packets.  Packet
    66	emission is isolated in `generate_nonlinear_packets.py`, and those packets are
    67	then checked by the shared target-blind guard before post-hoc target evaluation.
    68	
    69	The physical-model guard also emits no packets.  It should be replaced by a
    70	physical exporter only after the parent action and coupled residual equations
    71	are promoted and frozen in the ledger.
    72

     1	# Actual Branch Protocol V1
     2	
     3	This protocol is the next simulation handoff implied by the unincorporated
     4	5PN, barrier, atom, lepton, and `P22` notes.  It is not a candidate generator
     5	yet.  It freezes what a future physical moving-throat exporter must declare
     6	before any target residuals are evaluated.
     7	
     8	## Status
     9	
    10	The current executable simulation bundle shows that the reduced target-blind
    11	families and the manufactured nonlinear readiness family do not hit the target.
    12	The notes-intake guard in `diagnose_notes_intake.py` records the reason this is
    13	not a license to tune the current packets after the fact:
    14	
    15	- the 5PN handoff says the reduced theorem side is essentially closed;
    16	- the remaining task is an actual PDE-selected orbit-lock and outgoing branch;
    17	- support/source enhancement is not the active bottleneck in the reduced stack;
    18	- scalar support or scalar `P0` flux cannot be treated as direct `P22` or
    19	  `N2/N4` moment-shape control;
    20	- atom/lepton notes provide useful finite-throat source physics, but not a
    21	  calibrated actual-branch map into `D0`, `C`, `P0`, `N2`, and `N4`.

    23	## Frozen Inputs
    24	
    25	A future actual-branch exporter must freeze these items before target
    26	evaluation:
    27	
    28	| Item | Requirement |
    29	|---|---|
    30	| parent status | Declare strict `S_Sigma` promotion or explicitly label the wall equation as an effective closure |
    31	| geometry | Open finite-throat branch with `R_exit > 0`; no hard cap |
    32	| gauge and boundary class | Fixed before solve, with outgoing-port convention declared |
    33	| wall/support basis | Wall coordinates, BdG support basis, Maxwell/mixed ports, and extraction formulas |

    35	| source physics | Any leakage/work, `U/V` dressing, microscopic export, finite-throat `P0/P2`, scalar flux, and intrinsic `P22` terms included before residuals |
    36	| freeze hash | Complete protocol hash and source hashes attached to every exported packet |
    37

    39	
    40	The exporter must emit one or more target-blind packets with these fields.
    41

    44	For each grouped lane `A in {20, 21, 22}`:
    45

    69	```
    70

    83	## Target Quantities
    84	
    85	The simulation aliases are:
    86	
    87	```text
    88	D0 = K - B0 - Z0
    89	A  = -D2 = M + B2 + Z2
    90	C  = -D4 = B4 + Z4
    91	```
    92	
    93	The one-pole surface is:
    94	
    95	```text
    96	D0*C/(3*A^2) = 1
    97	```
    98	
    99	The outgoing prefactor moments are:
   100	
   101	```text
   102	P0 = N0/D0
   103	P2 = (D0*N2 + 2*A*N0)/D0^2
   104	P4 = (D0^2*N4 + 2*D0*(A*N2 + C*N0) + 3*A^2*N0)/D0^3
   105	```
   106	
   107	The constant-prefactor branch requires `P2 = 0` and `P4 = 0`, equivalently:
   108	
   109	```text
   110	N2 = -2*A*N0/D0
   111	N4 = N0*(A^2 - 2*D0*C)/D0^2
   112	```
   113	
   114	On the one-pole surface:
   115	
   116	```text
   117	N4 = -5*A^2*N0/D0^2
   118	```

   120	## Work Packages

     1	# Moving-Throat PDE — Stage 001 Geometry Lift and Linearized PDE Skeleton
     2	
     3	## 0. What this note does
     4	
     5	This is the first actual derivation move after the roadmap and Phase-0 theorem-target sheet.
     6	It does **not** try to solve the full nonlinear moving-throat problem.
     7	It fixes the first missing ingredient needed before any honest PDE work can proceed:
     8	
     9	1. an explicit **distributed throat geometry variable** replacing the current finite-dimensional `a(t), L(t)` closure,
    10	2. a **minimal linearized coupled bulk/interface system** for matter, gauge, and geometry,
    11	3. and a concrete **mode decomposition** in which the scalar lane, grouped real `P2` lane, and geometry lane become explicit.
    12	
    13	The key decision is to use a **hybrid level-set / shape-field representation**:
    14	
    15	- represent the finite throat surface by a level-set
    16	  
    17	  `Sigma(X,t)=0`,
    18	
    19	- but parameterize that level-set by a brane-spherical mouth shape field
    20	  
    21	  `r = R(Omega,w,t)`,
    22	
    23	  where `r = sqrt(x^2+y^2+z^2)` is the brane radius and `w` is the bulk axial direction.
    24	
    25	This is the smallest upgrade that keeps the 4D ontology intact while making the grouped real `P2` modes explicit.
    26	
    27	---
    28	
    29	## 1. Why this is the right geometry lift
    30	
    31	The existing parent theory already gives:
    32	
    33	- exact bulk GNLS matter,
    34	- exact localized `4+1` Maxwell,
    35	- and a geometry sector carried only by `a(t), L(t)` through `V_conf(X; a, L)`.
    36	
    37	That is enough for the reduced conservative hierarchy, but not enough for a genuine moving-throat PDE.
    38	
    39	The missing PDE must do three jobs simultaneously:
    40	
    41	1. make the current `a,L` variables emerge as collective moments,
    42	2. expose the conservative grouped real `P2` support/geometry channels explicitly,
    43	3. and provide the right mouth/worldtube response operator whose low-frequency data match the 2PN / 3PN / 2.5PN / 4PN ledgers.
    44	
    45	A pure collective-coordinate closure cannot do that.
    46	A pure abstract level-set `Sigma(X,t)` can do it, but hides the multipole structure.
    47	A pure moving-wall field `R(theta,phi,w,t)` makes the multipoles visible, but is less clean as a bulk coupling variable.
    48	
    49	So the right compromise is:
    50	
    51	`Sigma(x,y,z,w,t) = r - R(Omega,w,t)`
    52	
    53	with
    54	
    55	- `r = sqrt(x^2+y^2+z^2)`,
    56	- `Omega = x/r in S^2`,
    57	- the throat surface given by `Sigma=0`,
    58	- the exterior by `Sigma>0`,
    59	- the interior/support region by `Sigma<0`.
    60	
    61	This makes the mouth `S^2` harmonics explicit while preserving a level-set coupling to the bulk fields.
    62	
    63	Script-backed status:
    64	- `scripts/moving_throat_pde_stage001_geometry_lift_sympy_audit.py`
    65	  verifies the real-harmonic bookkeeping, confinement linearization sign, and
    66	  the densitized-versus-weighted wall-action convention used in this note.
    67	- `mathematica/moving_throat_pde_stage001_geometry_lift_mathematica_audit.wl`
    68	  mirrors the same symbolic checks in a second CAS so the foundational
    69	  harmonic, chain-rule, and wall-action bookkeeping is not resting on a single
    70	  engine.
    71	
    72	---
    73	
    74	## 2. Reference stationary throat background
    75	
    76	Take a stationary finite-throat reference surface
    77	
    78	`Sigma_0(X) = r - R_0(w) = 0`,
    79	
    80	with:
    81	
    82	- mouth at `w=0`,
    83	- finite throat depth `0 <= w <= L_0`,
    84	- reference mouth radius
    85	  
    86	  `a_0 = R_0(0)`,
    87	
    88	- and closure at the far end through either
    89	  
    90	  `R_0(L_0)=0`
    91	  
    92	  or an equivalent regular bottom condition.
    93	
    94	This is the minimal finite-throat geometry compatible with the already preferred finite branch and the D/N-style internal support picture.
    95	
    96	The current collective variables are recovered as monopole moments:
    97	
    98	`a(t) = (1/4pi) int_{S^2} R(Omega,0,t) dOmega`,
    99	
   100	and, if `W_b(Omega,t)` is the bottom location defined by `R(Omega,W_b(Omega,t),t)=0`,
   101	
   102	`L(t) = (1/4pi) int_{S^2} W_b(Omega,t) dOmega`.
   103	
   104	So the old `a(t),L(t)` survive, but only as the lowest geometry moments.
   105	
   106	---
   107	
   108	## 3. Promoted confinement coupling
   109	
   110	The old confinement potential is `V_conf(X; a, L)`.
   111	Promote it to a true moving-surface coupling by writing
   112	
   113	`V_conf(X; Sigma) = V_wall( Sigma(X,t) / ell_c )`,
   114	
   115	where `ell_c` is a wall-thickness / smoothing scale and `V_wall` is a steep profile.
   116	
   117	Then the stationary background is
   118	
   119	`V_0(X) = V_wall( Sigma_0(X) / ell_c )`.
   120	
   121	Linearizing gives
   122	
   123	`delta V_conf = (V_wall'(Sigma_0/ell_c)/ell_c) delta Sigma`.
   124	
   125	Since
   126	
   127	`Sigma = r - R(Omega,w,t)`,
   128	
   129	one has simply
   130	
   131	`delta Sigma = - delta R(Omega,w,t)`,
   132	
   133	so
   134	
   135	`delta V_conf = - (V_wall'(Sigma_0/ell_c)/ell_c) delta R`.
   136	
   137	This is the cleanest way to couple the moving throat directly to the bulk fields.
   138	
   139	---
   140	
   141	## 4. Mode decomposition of the throat geometry
   142	
   143	Write the geometry perturbation as
   144	
   145	`R(Omega,w,t) = R_0(w) + eta(Omega,w,t)`.
   146	
   147	Expand `eta` in real spherical harmonics on the brane mouth sphere:
   148	
   149	`eta(Omega,w,t) = eta_0(w,t) Y_00(Omega)`
   150	`                + sum_{m in P2(real)} q_{2m}(w,t) Y_{2m}^{real}(Omega)`
   151	`                + eta_{>=3}(Omega,w,t)`.
   152	
   153	The grouped real `P2` set is
   154	
   155	- `20`,
   156	- `21c`, `21s`,
   157	- `22c`, `22s`.
   158	
   159	This is the first place where the conservative grouped real `P2` lane becomes a literal geometry/support mode rather than a symbolic residual.
   160	
   161	Normalization note: with the standard normalized real harmonic
   162	
   163	`Y_00 = 1 / (2 sqrt(pi))`,
   164	
   165	all grouped real `P2` harmonics have zero sphere average, while
   166	
   167	`(1/4pi) int_{S^2} Y_00 dOmega = 1/(2 sqrt(pi))`.
   168	
   169	So the physical mouth-average monopole shift `delta a` is related to the normalized monopole coefficient by
   170	
   171	`q_00 = 2 sqrt(pi) delta a`.
   172	
   173	A useful further split is:
   174	
   175	`eta_0(w,t) = alpha_a(w) delta a(t) + alpha_L(w) delta L(t) + g(w,t)`,
   176	
   177	where:
   178	
   179	- `delta a` is the mouth-monopole radius shift,
   180	- `delta L` is the axial-depth / bottom shift,
   181	- `g(w,t)` is the remaining axisymmetric geometry lane orthogonal to the `a` and `L` moments.
   182	
   183	So the geometry sector separates into:
   184	
   185	1. `l=0` collective throat motion (`delta a`, `delta L`),
   186	2. `l=0` residual geometry lane `g`,
   187	3. grouped real `l=2` lanes `q_{2m}`,
   188	4. higher `l>=3` lanes.
   189	
   190	At the level of the current PN problem, the first serious nontrivial conservative payload is exactly the `l=2` bundle plus the axisymmetric geometry lane.
   191	
   192	---
   193	
   194	## 5. Minimal distributed geometry action (new ansatz)
   195	
   196	This part is **new** and is not yet frozen by the current papers. It is the smallest passive local action I would try first.
   197	
   198	Let `eta` be the radial wall displacement field above. Then take the quadratic geometry action
   199	
   200	`S_eta^(2) = (1/2) int dt dw dOmega sqrt(gamma_0)`
   201	`           [ mu_eta(w) (partial_t eta)^2`
   202	`             - T_w(w) (partial_w eta)^2`
   203	`             - T_Omega(w) eta (-Delta_{S^2}) eta`
   204	`             - K_eta(w) eta^2 ]`.
   205	
   206	Here:
   207	
   208	- `mu_eta(w)` is the effective wall inertia density,
   209	- `T_w(w)` is axial wall stiffness,
   210	- `T_Omega(w)` is angular stiffness on the mouth sphere,
   211	- `K_eta(w)` is a local restoring potential,
   212	- `gamma_0` is the metric determinant on the background throat surface.
   213	
   214	At this stage these are fixed effective constitutive functions of the chosen
   215	reference throat. The later derivation treats them as branch data to be computed
   216	or constrained, not as coefficients to be refit stage by stage to rescue the
   217	normalization chain.
   218	
   219	From this point onward, the modal equations are written in a densitized
   220	convention: after integrating over the reference sphere, the remaining
   221	background surface weight is absorbed into the effective one-dimensional
   222	coefficients `mu_eta, T_w, T_Omega, K_eta` and the wall amplitudes. Equivalently,
   223	the axial operator is written with respect to the flat measure `dw`. If one kept
   224	an explicit varying weight `g(w) = sqrt(gamma_0)`, the Euler-Lagrange equation
   225	would instead contain the extra first-derivative term `T_w g' q_w / g`.
   226	
   227	This is the minimal distributed upgrade that:
   228	
   229	- reduces to a genuine PDE in `w`,
   230	- makes the `S^2` multipole structure explicit,
   231	- and gives separate scalar and quadrupole restoring lanes automatically.
   232	
   233	Because
   234	
   235	`-Delta_{S^2} Y_{lm} = l(l+1) Y_{lm}`,
   236	
   237	this action yields the modal operator
   238	
   239	`mu_eta q_{lm,tt} - partial_w( T_w partial_w q_{lm} ) + [ K_eta + l(l+1) T_Omega ] q_{lm}`
   240	`= source_{lm}^{(psi,A)}`.
   240	`= source_{lm}^{(psi,A)}`.
   241	
   242	So the scalar lane `l=0` and grouped real `P2` lane `l=2` are already split before any further closure.
   243	
   244	This is exactly the structural feature the current hierarchy has been asking for.
   245	
   246	---
   247	
   248	## 6. Stationary background fields
   249	
   250	Choose a stationary finite-throat background
   251	
   252	`psi(X,t) = exp(-i mu_0 t / hbar) psi_0(X)`,
   253	
   254	`A_M(X,t) = A_{M0}(X)`,
   255	
   256	`R(Omega,w,t) = R_0(w)`.
   257	
   258	The background solves the exact parent bulk equations with the promoted confinement potential `V_0(X)`.
   259	
   260	At this stage, mixed channels must stay alive:
   261	
   262	- `A_w`,
   263	- `J^w`,
   264	- `F_{mu w}`,
   265	- `E_w`,
   266	- `C_a = F_{aw}`.
   267	
   268	They may decouple later on a far-field brane branch, but they must **not** be removed from the PDE that is supposed to generate the response data.
   269	
   270	---
   271	
   272	## 7. Linearized matter sector
   273	
   274	Write
   275	
   276	`psi = exp(-i mu_0 t/hbar) [ psi_0 + delta psi ]`,
   277	
   278	and define
   279	
   280	`delta rho = psi_0^* delta psi + psi_0 delta psi^*`.
   281	
   282	The linearized GNLS problem is naturally of Bogoliubov-de Gennes type:
   283	
   284	`i hbar partial_t [delta psi, delta psi^*]^T`
   285	`= L_BdG [delta psi, delta psi^*]^T`
   286	`  + C_A[delta A_M]`
   287	`  + C_eta[eta]`.
   288	
   289	A convenient explicit form is
   290	
   291	`H_0 = -(hbar^2/2m) D_{0i} D_0^i + V_0 + h(rho_0) - mu_0`,
   292	
   293	and then schematically
   294	
   295	`i hbar partial_t delta psi`
   296	`= H_0 delta psi + h'(rho_0) delta rho psi_0 + delta V_conf psi_0 + C_A^(+)[delta A]`,
   297	
   298	`-i hbar partial_t delta psi^*`
   299	`= H_0^* delta psi^* + h'(rho_0) delta rho psi_0^* + delta V_conf psi_0^* + C_A^(-)[delta A]`.
   300	
   301	Since
   302	
   303	`delta V_conf = - (V_wall'(Sigma_0/ell_c)/ell_c) eta`,
   304	
   305	the wall-displacement field enters the BdG system directly as the first moving-throat coupling.
   306	
   307	---
   308	
   309	## 8. Linearized gauge sector
   310	
   311	Write
   312	
   313	`A_M = A_{M0} + delta A_M`.
   314	
   315	Linearizing the exact localized Maxwell equation gives
   316	
   317	`partial_M [ Z(w) delta F^{MN} ] + (1/xi) partial^N (partial . delta A)`
   318	`= mu_0 delta J^N`.
   319	
   320	The linearized current is the exact first variation of the minimally coupled matter current. In schematic form,
   321	
   322	`delta J^0 = q_* delta rho`,
   323	
   324	`delta J^i = q_* delta j^i`,
   325	
   326	with
   327	
   328	`delta j^i = (hbar/m) Im( psi_0^* D_0^i delta psi + delta psi^* D_0^i psi_0 )`
   329	`           - (q_*/m) rho_0 delta A^i`
   330	`           + ...`.
   331	
   332	The important point is not the final algebraic form but the channel content:
   333	
   334	- `delta A_w` survives,
   335	- `delta J^w` survives,
   336	- `delta F_{mu w}` survives.
   337	
   338	So the PDE can actually test whether the mixed channels that were suppressed in the brane limit are part of the microscopic response law.
   339	
   340	---
   341	
   342	## 9. Linearized geometry equation
   343	
   344	Varying the new quadratic geometry action and coupling to the matter/gauge sectors gives the geometry PDE
   345	
   346	`mu_eta partial_t^2 eta - partial_w( T_w partial_w eta ) - T_Omega Delta_{S^2} eta + K_eta eta`
   347	`= S_eta^(psi)[delta psi,delta psi^*] + S_eta^(A)[delta A_M] + f_ext`.
   348	
   349	At the linearized level, the first source term from the confinement coupling is generated by
   350	
   351	`delta V_conf = - (V_wall'(Sigma_0/ell_c)/ell_c) eta`,
   352	
   353	so the matter back-reaction contributes through the linearized generalized force
   354	
   355	`S_eta^(psi) ~ - (V_wall'(Sigma_0/ell_c)/ell_c) delta rho + ...`.
   356	
   357	Projecting onto spherical harmonics gives mode equations
   358	
   359	`mu_eta q_{lm,tt} - partial_w( T_w partial_w q_{lm} )`
   360	`+ [ K_eta + l(l+1) T_Omega ] q_{lm}`
   361	`= S_{lm}^{(psi,A)} + f_{lm}^{ext}`.
   362	
   363	This is the first usable linearized moving-throat PDE family.
   364	
   365	---
   366	
   367	## 10. The first mode sectors that matter
   368	
   369	For the present program, the important sectors are:
   370	
   371	### `l = 0` axisymmetric sector
   372	
   373	This contains:
   374	
   375	- `delta a(t)`,
   376	- `delta L(t)`,
   377	- the residual geometry lane `g(w,t)`.
   378	
   379	This is the lane that should eventually reproduce the symbolic geometry completion / scalar-response structures left open in the lower-order hierarchy.
   380	
   381	### grouped real `l = 2` sector
   382	
   383	This contains
   384	
   385	- `q_20(w,t)`,
   386	- `q_21c(w,t)`, `q_21s(w,t)`,
   387	- `q_22c(w,t)`, `q_22s(w,t)`.
   388	
   389	On an exactly isotropic reference throat, these are degenerate at the geometry-only level.
   390	Any splitting among the grouped channels then measures anisotropy induced by matter support, gauge support, or wall structure.
   391	
   392	This is exactly the conservative information the 3PN grouped real `P2` closure needs.
   393	
   394	### higher `l >= 3` sector
   395	
   396	These modes should be kept in the full PDE, but they are not needed in the first reduced theorem target.
   397	
   398	---
   399	
   400	## 11. Mouth/worldtube response operator in the new variables
   401	
   402	At the mouth `w = 0`, choose a real harmonic port basis
   403	
   404	- `P_00 = Y_00`,
   405	- `P_20`, `P_21c`, `P_21s`, `P_22c`, `P_22s`.
   406	
   407	Then define effort variables by projecting the drive on the mouth/worldtube,
   408	for example:
   409	
   410	- scalar enthalpy drive `u_0(omega)`,
   411	- grouped real `P2` drives `u_{2m}(omega)`,
   412	- optional geometry drive `u_g(omega)`.
   413	
   414	Define measured fluxes as the matching projected normal fluxes / generalized tractions,
   415	for example:
   416	
   417	- matter flux through the mouth,
   418	- leakage flux in `w`,
   419	- wall traction `T_w partial_w q_{lm}` at the mouth,
   420	- grouped support amplitudes.
   421	
   422	Then the response operator is
   423	
   424	`j_A(omega) = sum_B Z_eff,AB(omega) u_B(omega)`.
   425	
   426	For an isotropic background this should block-diagonalize into
   427	
   428	- scalar/geometry block,
   429	- grouped real `P2` block,
   430	- higher-`l` blocks.
   431	
   432	The grouped `P2` block is the one that eventually feeds
   433	
   434	- `u2^(20), u2^(21), u2^(22)`,
   435	- isotropy defects,
   436	- and the canonical pair `(Kbar_0, Kbar_2)` on the passive/outgoing quadrupole branch.
   437

   464

   466

   468

   470

   472

   492

   494	
   495	The old `a(t),L(t)` remain present, but only as the lowest collective moments of a genuine distributed geometry field.
   496	That is the right relationship between the old reduced hierarchy and the new PDE.
   497	
   498	### Advantage 4 — it is the smallest passive distributed geometry action that can work
   499	
   500	The quadratic wall action above is the smallest honest PDE upgrade I know that automatically separates:
   501	
   502	- scalar/geometry,
   503	- grouped real `P2`,

   506	That is precisely the structure the current hierarchy has been trying to expose.

    29	  S_\eta^{(2)}
    30	  =
    31	  \frac12\int dt\,dw\,d\Omega\,
    32	  \Big[
    33	  \mu_\eta \eta_t^2
    34	  -T_w\eta_w^2
    35	  -T_\Omega\eta(-\Delta_{S^2})\eta
    36	  -K_\eta\eta^2
    37	  \Big]
    38	  \]
    39	  is included, then the advertised moving-wall PDE, boundary terms, modal split, and positivity gates are mathematically consistent.
    40	
    41	So V2-01 has a **split verdict**:
    42	
    43	\[
    44	\boxed{
    45	\text{Strict parent-level moving-throat claim: not yet passed.}
    46	}
    47	\]
    48	
    49	\[
    50	\boxed{
    51	\text{Linear effective wall-closure algebra: passed.}
    52	}
    53	\]
    54	
    55	This is not a fatal flaw. It is a status correction. The program should either:
    56	
    57	1. promote \(S_\eta\), or better a nonlinear \(S_\Sigma\), into the declared parent action, or  
    58	2. explicitly label the moving-wall PDE as an effective closure until the parent throat action is derived.
    59	
    60	---
    61	
    62	## Source anchors
    63	
    64	The compact program currently lists the core fields as \(\psi,A_M,\Sigma\) or \(R\), but its exact parent action is written as GNLS plus localized Maxwell, with geometry entering through \(V_{\rm conf}(\mathbf X;\Sigma)\). The same compact ledger also tags the moving-throat lift as a closure hierarchy rather than a completed branch theorem.
    65	
    66	The Stage-1 geometry lift explicitly introduces the distributed wall action as a **new ansatz** and says the existing parent theory has exact GNLS, exact localized Maxwell, and a geometry sector previously carried only by \(a(t),L(t)\) through \(V_{\rm conf}\). The full derivation ledger later shows that the distributed wall lift is compatible with the old \(a,L\) closure, but still treats the later matter/gauge/outgoing realizations as reduced theorem work rather than a solved nonlinear moving-throat theorem.
    67	
    68	---
    69	
    70	## 1. Audit target
    71	
    72	The ideal parent-level statement would be
    73	
    74	\[
    75	S_{\rm total}=S_\psi+S_{\rm EM}+S_\Sigma,
    76	\]
    77	
    78	with \(S_\Sigma\) supplying the dynamics of the moving throat.
    79	
    80	The current compact parent action instead has the schematic form
    81	
    82	\[
    83	S_{\rm current}
    84	=
    85	\int dt\,d^4X\,
    86	\left[
    87	\mathcal L_\psi(\psi,A;\Sigma)
    88	+
    89	\mathcal L_{\rm EM}(A)
    90	\right],
    91	\]
    92	
    93	where
    94	
    95	\[
    96	\mathcal L_\psi
    97	=
    98	\frac{i\hbar}{2}
    99	(\psi^\ast D_t\psi-\psi D_t\psi^\ast)
   100	-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}(D_i\psi)^\ast(D_i\psi)
   101	-V_{\rm conf}(\mathbf X;\Sigma)\rho
   102	-U(\rho).
   103	\]
   104	
   105	Thus \(\Sigma\) appears through \(V_{\rm conf}\), but there is no term of the form
   106	
   107	\[
   108	\Sigma_t^2,\quad
   109	|\nabla\Sigma|^2,\quad
   110	\eta_t^2,\quad
   111	\eta_w^2,\quad
   112	\eta(-\Delta_{S^2})\eta,
   113	\]
   114	
   115	unless the wall action is added separately.
   116	
   117	---
   118	
   119	## 2. Variation of the confinement-only parent term
   120	
   121	Use the moving-surface representation
   122	
   123	\[
   124	\Sigma=r-R(\Omega,w,t),
   125	\qquad
   126	R=R_0+\eta.
   127	\]
   128	
   129	Take
   130	
   131	\[
   132	V_{\rm conf}
   133	=
   134	V_{\rm wall}\!\left(\frac{\Sigma}{\ell_c}\right).
   135	\]
   136	
   137	Linearizing around the background gives
   138	
   139	\[
   140	\delta\Sigma=-\eta,
   141	\]
   142	
   143	so
   144	
   145	\[
   146	\delta V_{\rm conf}
   147	=
   148	-\frac{V_{\rm wall}'(\Sigma_0/\ell_c)}{\ell_c}\eta.
   149	\]
   150	
   151	Since the matter Lagrangian contains
   152	
   153	\[
   154	-\rho V_{\rm conf},
   155	\]
   156	
   157	the linearized wall-dependent contribution is
   158	
   159	\[
   160	\delta\mathcal L_\psi
   161	=
   162	+\rho\frac{V_{\rm wall}'(\Sigma_0/\ell_c)}{\ell_c}\eta.
   163	\]
   164	
   165	Therefore the Euler derivative with respect to \(\eta\) is only
   166	
   167	\[
   168	\frac{\delta \mathcal L_\psi}{\delta\eta}
   169	=
   170	\rho\frac{V_{\rm wall}'(\Sigma_0/\ell_c)}{\ell_c}.
   171	\]
   172	
   173	There are no terms proportional to
   174	
   175	\[
   176	\eta_{tt},\qquad
   177	\partial_w(T_w\eta_w),\qquad
   178	\Delta_{S^2}\eta.
   179	\]
   180	
   181	So the confinement-only parent action gives a force/source term. It does **not** give an autonomous moving-throat PDE.
   182	
   183	This is the core V2-01 result.
   184	
   185	---
   186	
   187	## 3. Variation after adding the quadratic wall action
   188	
   189	Now add the modal wall Lagrangian
   190	
   191	\[
   192	L_{\ell m}
   193	=
   194	\frac12\mu_\eta q_{\ell m,t}^2
   195	-\frac12T_w q_{\ell m,w}^2
   196	-\frac12
   197	\left[
   198	K_\eta+\ell(\ell+1)T_\Omega
   199	\right]q_{\ell m}^2
   200	+S_{\ell m}q_{\ell m}.
   201	\]
   202	
   203	The Euler-Lagrange expression is
   204	
   205	\[
   206	\frac{\partial L}{\partial q}
   207	-\partial_t\frac{\partial L}{\partial q_t}
   208	-\partial_w\frac{\partial L}{\partial q_w}
   209	=0.
   210	\]
   211	
   212	This gives
   213	
   214	\[
   215	-\left[
   216	\mu_\eta q_{\ell m,tt}
   217	-\partial_w(T_w q_{\ell m,w})
   218	+
   219	(K_\eta+\ell(\ell+1)T_\Omega)q_{\ell m}
   220	-S_{\ell m}
   221	\right]=0.
   222	\]
   223	
   224	Equivalently,
   225	
   226	\[
   227	\boxed{
   228	\mu_\eta q_{\ell m,tt}
   229	-\partial_w(T_w q_{\ell m,w})
   230	+
   231	\left[
   232	K_\eta+\ell(\ell+1)T_\Omega
   233	\right]q_{\ell m}
   234	=
   235	S_{\ell m}.
   236	}
   237	\]

     1	# Stage V2-16 — Branch-freeze / no-refit protocol
     2	
     3	## Purpose
     4	
     5	This stage turns the anti-overfitting rule into an executable theorem gate.
     6	
     7	The problem is not that the grouped `P2` algebra lacks enough variables. It has many. The problem is that, unless the branch is frozen before comparison, the same algebra contains enough freedom to make target matching look stronger than it is.
     8	
     9	The rule for Volume 2 is therefore:
    10	
    11	> Define the parent action, gauge convention, wall/interface action, open-exit boundary protocol, projection/source map, support-profile family, number of modes/ports, stability gates, and extraction formulas **before** evaluating any target residual.
    12	
    13	Then, and only then, evaluate the residual packet.
    14	
    15	---
    16	
    17	## 1. Frozen protocol DAG
    18	
    19	The stage encodes the protocol as a directed acyclic graph:
    20	
    21	```text
    22	parent_action
    23	  -> gauge_convention
    24	  -> wall_action_and_geometry
    25	  -> open_boundary_protocol
    26	  -> projection_and_source_map
    27	  -> support_profile_family
    28	  -> branch_solve
    29	  -> coefficient_extraction
    30	  -> target_residual_evaluation
    31	  -> target_decision
    32	```
    33	
    34	The audit verifies three graph facts:
    35	
    36	1. all allowed arrows point forward in the frozen order;
    37	2. there is no path from target residuals or target decisions back into branch definitions;
    38	3. a deliberately bad edge,
    39	   ```text
    40	   target_residual_evaluation -> support_profile_family
    41	   ```

     3	## Status
     4	
     5	This stage is a **pre-solver theorem gate**, not a nonlinear branch solution.
     6	
     7	The previous stages collapsed the isotropic grouped-\(P_2\) finish line to one scalar normalization test,
     8	
     9	\[
    10	\widehat m_0^{\,2}\mathcal S_{\rm port}\frac{N_0}{D_0}
    11	=
    12	\frac{54Gc_s^5}{5a^5c^5},
    13	\]
    14	
    15	together with conservative one-pole, constant-prefactor, tail-transport, stability, and freeze-order gates.
    16	
    17	V2-20 answers the next practical question:
    18	
    19	> When a future moving-throat solver outputs a branch, exactly what weak-form data must be extracted, and how do we turn those data into \(K,M,B_n,Z_n,N_n,\widehat m_0,\Theta_{\rm tail}\) without refitting the target?
    20	
    21	## Architectural patch retained from V2-04
    22	
    23	The throat is now treated as an **open finite-radius conduit**.
    24	
    25	The exit data are:
    26	
    27	\[
    28	R(L)>0,
    29	\]
    30	
    31	not
    32	
    33	\[
    34	R(L)=0.
    35	\]
    36	
    37	The AC support modes may see an effective Neumann condition through an open-exit impedance mismatch, but this is not a hard geometric cap. The zero/DC superfluid current is allowed to exit and is recorded through the open-system leakage bookkeeping rather than through the finite-support AC mode equation.
    38	
    39	In this stage, the far end is represented by a Robin/impedance condition,
    40	
    41	\[
    42	T_w q_w(L,\omega)+Y_L(\omega)q(L,\omega)=0.
    43	\]
    44	
    45	The Neumann support limit is
    46	
    47	\[
    48	Y_L(\omega)\to0.
    49	\]
    50	
    51	For a low-impedance open expansion, this is the support-coordinate version of the organ-pipe reflection result from V2-04.
    52	
    53	## 1. Weak form for one wall harmonic
    54	
    55	For a real harmonic sector \((l,m)\), write
    56	
    57	\[
    58	V_l(w)=K_\eta(w)+l(l+1)T_\Omega(w).
    59	\]
    60	
    61	The densitized wall equation is
    62	
    63	\[
    64	\mu_\eta q_{tt}
    65	-\partial_w(T_w q_w)
    66	+V_l q
    67	=
    68	S_l.
    69	\]
    70	
    71	Using \(q(w,t)=q(w,\omega)e^{-i\omega t}\), this becomes
    72	
    73	\[
    74	-\omega^2\mu_\eta q
    75	-\partial_w(T_w q_w)
    76	+V_lq
    77	=
    78	S_l.
    79	\]
    80	
    81	For a test function \(\varphi\) satisfying the mouth constraint, the weak form is
    82	
    83	\[
    84	\int_0^L
    85	\left[
    86	T_w q_w\varphi_w
    87	+
    88	(V_l-\omega^2\mu_\eta)q\varphi
    89	\right]dw
    90	+
    91	Y_L(\omega)q(L)\varphi(L)
    92	=
    93	\int_0^L S_l\varphi\,dw.
    94	\]
    95	
    96	The SymPy script verifies the integration-by-parts identity
    97	
    98	\[
    99	Tq_w\varphi_w-\partial_w(Tq_w\varphi)
   100	=
   101	-\partial_w(Tq_w)\varphi.
   102	\]
   103	
   104	It also verifies the open-exit sign convention: the endpoint variation is
   105	
   106	\[
   107	\left[T_w q_w(L)+Y_Lq(L)\right]\varphi(L),
   108	\]
   109	
   110	so free exit variations impose
   111	
   112	\[
   113	T_w q_w(L)+Y_Lq(L)=0.
   114	\]
   115	
   116	## 2. Galerkin extraction matrices
   117	
   118	Choose a frozen branch basis \(\{\chi_i(w)\}\) satisfying the mouth condition. In a numerical solver this basis may be finite elements, splines, spectral functions, or computed eigenfunctions. The extracted matrices are
   119	
   120	\[
   121	M_{ij}^{(l)}
   122	=
   123	\int_0^L\mu_\eta(w)\chi_i(w)\chi_j(w)\,dw,
   124	\]
   125	
   126	\[
   127	K_{ij}^{(l)}
   128	=
   129	\int_0^L
   130	\left[
   131	T_w(w)\chi_i'(w)\chi_j'(w)
   132	+
   133	V_l(w)\chi_i(w)\chi_j(w)
   134	\right]dw
   135	+
   136	Y_L(0)\chi_i(L)\chi_j(L).
   137	\]
   138	
   139	The script checks a two-function Dirichlet-mouth open-exit toy basis,
   140	
   141	\[
   142	\chi_1=w/L,\qquad \chi_2=(w/L)^2,
   143	\]
   144	
   145	and derives
   146	
   147	\[
   148	M
   149	=
   150	\begin{pmatrix}
   151	L\mu/3 & L\mu/4\\
   152	L\mu/4 & L\mu/5
   153	\end{pmatrix},
   154	\qquad
   155	\det M=\frac{L^2\mu^2}{240}>0.
   156	\]
   157	
   158	The stiffness matrix is symmetric and is positive in the tested positive-coefficient sample.
   159	
   160	For the AC support limit \(Y_L\to0\), the same script checks the D/N support seed,
   161	
   162	\[
   163	q(w)=\sin\left(\frac{\pi w}{2L}\right),
   164	\]
   165

   168	\[
   169	q(0)=0,\qquad q_w(L)=0.
   170	\]
   171	
   172	This keeps the support ladder while avoiding a capped geometry.

     2	
     3	## 0. Purpose
     4	
     5	This stage turns the Volume 2 weak-form scaffold into an executable branch-extraction fixture.
     6	
     7	The fixture does **not** solve the nonlinear moving-throat PDE.     38	      "name": "branch name",
    39	      "geometry": {
    40	        "R_exit": 0.35,
    41	        "boundary_class": "open_impedance",
    42	        "Y_L_limit": 0.0
    43	      },
    44	      "target": {
    45	        "constants": {
    46	          "G": 1.0,
    47	          "c_s": 1.0,
    48	          "c": 1.0,
    49	          "a": 1.0,
    50	          "mhat0": 1.0,
    51	          "S_port": 1.0,
    52	          "theta_tail": 1.0
    53	        }
    54	      },
    55	      "lanes": {
    56	        "20": { "...": "lane data" },
    57	        "21": { "...": "lane data" },
    58	        "22": { "...": "lane data" }
    59	      }
    60	    }
    61	  ]
    62	}
    63	```
    64	
    65	Each grouped lane may be supplied in either of two ways.
    66	
    67	### 1.1 Primitive reduced-mode input
    68	
    69	```json
    70	{
    71	  "K": 1.6,
    72	  "M": 0.9,

    77	    {"Omega_U": 3.0, "Omega_W": 4.0, "R": 0.65, "g_U": 0.28, "g_W": 0.52}

   101	
   102	The direct-coefficient path is included only as an algebraic self-test and for importing future pre-extracted numerical coefficients. The primitive path is the intended route for real branch data.
   103	
   104	---
   105	
   106	## 2. Open-throat gate
   107	
   108	The fixture enforces the open-organ-pipe patch by requiring
   109	
   110	\[
   111	R_{\rm exit}>0,
   112	\]
   113	
   114	and
   115	
   116	\[
   117	\texttt{boundary\_class}=\texttt{open\_impedance}.
   118	\]
   119	
   120	It rejects or fails hard-cap geometry:
   121	
   122	\[
   123	R(L)=0
   124	\]
   125	
   126	as a branch-realization condition for the support problem. In this fixture, the support-mode Neumann-like condition is represented by the open impedance limit
   127	
   128	\[
   129	T_w q_w(L,\omega)+Y_L(\omega)q(L,\omega)=0,
   130	\qquad
   131	Y_L\to0
   132	\]
   133	
   134	for AC support modes, while DC leakage is allowed through the finite exit.
   135	
   136	---
   137	
   138	## 3. Lane-level extraction formulas
   139	
   140	For each grouped lane
   141	
   142	\[
   143	A\in\{20,21,22\},
   144	\]
   145	
   146	the fixture computes BdG moments, Maxwell/mixed moments, outgoing-transfer moments, conservative operator moments, response moments, and prefactor moments.
   147	
   148	### 3.1 BdG support moments
   149	
   150	For stable positive-energy support coordinates with couplings \(c_\alpha\) and frequencies \(\varpi_\alpha>0\),
   151	
   152	\[
   153	B_0=\sum_\alpha \frac{c_\alpha^2}{\varpi_\alpha^2},
   154	\]
   155	
   156	\[
   157	B_2=\sum_\alpha \frac{c_\alpha^2}{\varpi_\alpha^4},
   158	\]
   159	
   160	\[
   161	B_4=\sum_\alpha \frac{c_\alpha^2}{\varpi_\alpha^6}.
   162	\]
   163	
   164	These are the Schur-complement support moments from the stable BdG closure.
   165	
   166	### 3.2 Conservative Maxwell/mixed moments
   167	
   168	For a port with
   169	
   170	\[
   171	\Omega_U,
   172	\qquad
   173	\Omega_W,
   174	\qquad
   175	R,
   176	\qquad
   177	g_U,
   178	\qquad
   179	g_W,
   180	\]
   181	
   182	define
   183	
   184	\[
   185	\Delta=\Omega_U^2\Omega_W^2-R^2,
   186	\]
   187	
   188	\[
   189	S=\Omega_U^2+\Omega_W^2,
   190	\]
   191	
   192	\[
   193	Q=g_U^2\Omega_W^2+2g_Ug_WR+g_W^2\Omega_U^2,
   194	\]
   195	
   196	\[
   197	H=g_U^2+g_W^2.
   198	\]
   199	
   200	Then
   201	
   202	\[
   203	Z_0=\frac{Q}{\Delta},
   204	\]
   205	
   206	\[
   207	Z_2=\frac{QS-H\Delta}{\Delta^2},
   208	\]
   209	
   210	\[
   211	Z_4=\frac{Q(S^2-\Delta)-SH\Delta}{\Delta^3}.
   212	\]
   213	
   214	For multiple mixed ports, the fixture sums these contributions over ports.
   215	
   216	### 3.3 Outgoing-transfer moments
   217	
   218	Define the outgoing-port numerator
   219	
   220	\[
   221	P=\Omega_U^2g_W+Rg_U.
   222	\]
   223	
   224	Then
   225	
   226	\[
   227	N_0=\frac{P^2}{\Delta^2},
   228	\]
   229	
   230	\[
   231	N_2=\frac{2P(PS-\Delta g_W)}{\Delta^3},
   232	\]
   233	
   234	\[
   235	N_4=
   236	\frac{
   237	\Delta^2 g_W^2
   238	-2\Delta P^2
   239	-4\Delta PSg_W
   240	+3P^2S^2
   241	}{\Delta^4}.
   242	\]
   243	
   244	Again, for multiple ports, the fixture sums over ports.
   245	
   246	### 3.4 Conservative wall operator
   247	
   248	The lane operator moments are
   249	
   250	\[
   251	D_0=K-B_0-Z_0,
   252	\]
   253	
   254	\[
   255	D_2=-(M+B_2+Z_2),
   256	\]
   257	
   258	\[
   259	D_4=-(B_4+Z_4).
   260	\]
     1	# Stage V2-23 — Minimal open-throat branch solver and first real residual extraction
     2	
     3	## 0. Purpose
     4	
     5	This stage is the first reduced branch-realization prototype after the V2-22C
     6	handoff pipeline.
     7	
     8	It is **not** a full nonlinear GNLS/Maxwell/moving-wall PDE solution. It is a
     9	target-blind, frozen, one-dimensional open-throat branch solve that moves beyond
    10	mock profiles by solving:
    11	
    12	1. a stationary finite-radius open throat profile,
    13	2. a wall `l=2` Sturm-Liouville support profile,
    14	3. a stable BdG support profile,
    15	4. a brane-like localized gauge profile,
    16	5. a mixed `A_w/F_{\mu w}/J^w` profile,
    17	
    18	then computing overlap integrals and passing the resulting branch through the
    19	same isotropic full-bundle residual packet used in V2-19 through V2-22C.
    20	
    21	The branch is intentionally simple. Its job is to give Codex/local solvers a
    22	concrete executable template for the next full PDE branch export.
    23	
    24	## 1. Frozen branch definition
    25	
    26	```text
    27	branch_id: v2_23_minimal_open_throat_frozen_demo
    28	branch_freeze_hash: 0feee821ffec9b23f79d80bb4e176139f01fbffb3f1358607dad6597032592ae
    29	pre_target_freeze: true
    30	target_blind: true
    31	no_post_residual_refit: true
    32	boundary_class: open_impedance
    33	boundary_protocol: open_impedance_AC_reflecting_DC_leaking
    34	```
    35	
    36	The geometry is an open finite throat, not a capped tube:
    37	
    38	\[
    39	R(0)=a,\qquad R(L)>0.
    40	\]
    41	
    42	The stationary profile is obtained by minimizing
    43	
    44	\[
    45	E[R]
    46	=
    47	\frac12\int_0^L T_R (R')^2\,ds
    48	+
    49	\frac12\int_0^L K_R(R-R_{\rm pref})^2\,ds
    50	+
    51	\frac12Y_{\rm exit}(R(L)-R_{\rm exit,pref})^2,
    52	\]
    53	
    54	with fixed mouth radius \(R(0)=a\). The exit condition is a finite-radius open
    55	penalty rather than a cap.
    56	
    57	The solved branch gives
    58	
    59	\[
    60	R_{\rm mouth}=1,\qquad
    61	R_{\rm exit}=0.452938042901,\qquad
    62	R_{\rm min}=0.452938042901.
    63	\]
    64	
    65	The open gate passes because \(R_{\rm exit}>0\).
    66	
    67	## 2. Axial measure
    68	
    69	The solver uses the geometry-derived effective axial measure
    70	
    71	\[
    72	\mu_s(s)=R_0(s)^2\sqrt{1+R_0'(s)^2},
    73	\]
    74	
    75	renormalized so that
    76	
    77	\[
    78	\int_0^L\mu_s(s)\,ds=L.
    79	\]
    80	
    81	This remains a reduced one-dimensional model, but the overlap integrals now
    82	depend on the solved open-throat geometry rather than on a flat hand-inserted
    83	measure.
    84	
    85	## 3. Solved Sturm-Liouville problems
    86	
    87	Each profile is obtained from a finite-element Sturm-Liouville problem
    88	
    89	\[
    90	-\partial_s(T(s)\partial_s q)+V(s)q=\lambda\mu_s(s)q,
    91	\]
    92	
    93	with mouth Dirichlet condition
    94	
    95	\[
    96	q(0)=0,
    97	\]
    98	
    99	and open-end impedance condition
   100	
   101	\[
   102	T(L)q'(L)+Y_Lq(L)=0.
   103	\]
   104	
   105	For this first branch prototype the AC-reflecting organ-pipe limit is used:
   106	
   107	\[
   108	Y_L=0,
   109	\]
   110	
   111	so the exit is Neumann-like for AC support modes while remaining geometrically
   112	open for DC/background flow.
   113	
   114	The solved eigenvalues are:
   115	
   116	\[
   117	K=\lambda_{{\rm wall},l=2}=2.2393180779,
   118	\]
   119	
   120	\[
   121	\varpi^2=3.16919632623,
   122	\]
   123	
   124	\[
   125	\Omega_U^2=3.78509395487,\qquad
   126	\Omega_W^2=4.05724378721.
   127	\]
   128	
   129	The FEM residuals are reported in `stage_v2_23_tolerance_report.json`.
   130	
   131	## 4. Overlap integrals
   132	
   133	The reduced overlap integrals are
   134	
   135	\[
   136	I_{\eta\phi}=\int_0^L\mu_s\chi_\eta\phi\,ds,
   137	\]
   138	
   139	\[
   140	I_{\eta U}=\int_0^L\mu_s\chi_\eta u\,ds,
   141	\]
   142	
   143	\[
   144	I_{\eta W}=\int_0^L\mu_s\chi_\eta w\,ds,
   145	\]
   146	
   147	\[
   148	I_{UW}=\int_0^L\mu_s u w\,ds.
   149	\]
   150	
   151	For this frozen branch,
   152	
   153	\[
   154	I_{\eta\phi}=0.999946613757,
   155	\qquad
   156	I_{\eta U}=0.999180452256,
   157	\]
   158	
   159	\[
   160	I_{\eta W}=0.994783990782,
   161	\qquad
   162	I_{UW}=0.998096444041.
   163	\]
   164	
   165	The reduced couplings are
   166	
   167	\[
   168	c_B=\lambda_B I_{\eta\phi},
   169	\qquad
   170	g_U=\lambda_U I_{\eta U},
   171	\qquad
   172	g_W=\lambda_W I_{\eta W},
   173	\qquad
   174	R=\lambda_R I_{UW}.
   175	\]
   176	
   177	## 5. Reduced coefficients
   178	
   179	The stable BdG contribution is
   180	
   181	\[
   182	B_0=\frac{c_B^2}{\varpi^2},
   183	\qquad
   184	B_2=\frac{c_B^2}{\varpi^4},
   185	\qquad
   186	B_4=\frac{c_B^2}{\varpi^6}.
   187	\]
   188	
   189	The conservative Maxwell/mixed block uses
   190	
   191	\[
   192	\Delta=\Omega_U^2\Omega_W^2-R^2,
   193	\]
   194	
   195	\[
   196	Q=g_U^2\Omega_W^2+2g_Ug_WR+g_W^2\Omega_U^2,
   197	\]
   198	
   199	\[
   200	H=g_U^2+g_W^2,\qquad
   201	S=\Omega_U^2+\Omega_W^2.
   202	\]
   203	
   204	Then
   205	
   206	\[
   207	Z_0=\frac Q\Delta,
   208	\]
   209	
   210	\[
   211	Z_2=\frac{QS-H\Delta}{\Delta^2},
   212	\]
   213	
   214	\[
   215	Z_4=\frac{Q(S^2-\Delta)-SH\Delta}{\Delta^3}.
   216	\]
   217	
   218	The outgoing-transfer moments are
   219	
   220	\[
   221	N_0=\frac{(\Omega_U^2g_W+Rg_U)^2}{\Delta^2},
   222	\]
   223	
   224	\[
   225	N_2=
   226	\frac{2P(P S-\Delta g_W)}{\Delta^3},
   227	\qquad
   228	P=\Omega_U^2g_W+Rg_U,
   229	\]
   230	
   231	\[
   232	N_4=
   233	\frac{\Delta^2g_W^2-2\Delta P^2-4\Delta PSg_W+3P^2S^2}{\Delta^4}.
   234	\]
   235	
   236	The total conservative operator is
   237	
   238	\[
   239	D_0=K-B_0-Z_0,
   240	\]
   241	
   242	\[
   243	D_2=-(M+B_2+Z_2),
   244	\]
   245	
   246	\[
   247	D_4=-(B_4+Z_4).
   248	\]
   249	
   250	The solved branch gives
   251	
   252	\[
   253	D_0=1.89448908712,\qquad
   254	D_2=-1.09827027208,\qquad
   255	D_4=-0.0282005090292.
   256	\]
   257	
   258	## 6. Observable packet
   259	
   260	The normalized response and outgoing prefactor are
   261	
   262	\[
   263	u_2=-\frac{D_2}{D_0},
   264	\]
   265	
   266	\[
   267	u_4=\frac{D_2^2-D_0D_4}{D_0^2},
   268	\]
   269	
   270	\[
   271	P_0=\frac{N_0}{D_0},
   272	\]
   273	
   274	\[
   275	P_2=\frac{D_0N_2-2D_2N_0}{D_0^2},
   276	\]
   277	
   278	\[
   279	P_4=
   280	\frac{D_0^2N_4-2D_0(D_2N_2+D_4N_0)+3D_2^2N_0}{D_0^3}.
   281	\]
   282	
   283	For this branch,
   284	
   285	\[
   286	u_2=0.579718447339,\qquad
   287	u_4=0.350959026601,
   288	\]
   289	
   290	\[
   291	P_0=0.0197851167073,\qquad
   292	P_2=0.0332589572512,\qquad

    48	
    49	## 2. Coefficient map
    50	
    51	On the isotropic grouped real `P2` branch, write the conservative denominator
    52	and outgoing numerator as
    53	
    54	```text
    55	D(omega) = D0 + D2 omega^2 + D4 omega^4 + O(omega^6),
    56	N(omega) = N0 + N2 omega^2 + N4 omega^4 + O(omega^6).
    57	```
    58	
    59	The full-bundle aliases are
    60	
    61	```text
    62	D0 = K - B0 - Z0,
    63	D2 = -(M + B2 + Z2),
    64	D4 = -(B4 + Z4).
    65	```
    66	
    67	Equivalently,
    68	
    69	```text
    70	A = M + B2 + Z2 = -D2,
    71	C = B4 + Z4 = -D4.
    72	```
    73	
    74	Here:
    75	
    76	- `K,M` are wall/worldtube stiffness and inertia data;
    77	- `B0,B2,B4` are stable BdG support moments;
    78	- `Z0,Z2,Z4` are conservative Maxwell/mixed moments;
    79	- `N0,N2,N4` are outgoing-transfer moments.
    80	
    81	The normalized conservative response is
    82	
    83	```text
    84	Y(omega) = D0 / D(omega)
    85	         = 1 + u2 omega^2 + u4 omega^4 + O(omega^6),
    86	```
    87	
    88	with
    89	
    90	```text
    91	u2 = A/D0,
    92	u4 = (A^2 + D0*C)/D0^2.
    93	```
    94	
    95	The one-pole condition is `u4 = 4 u2^2`, so
    96	
    97	```text
    98	D0*C = 3*A^2,
    99	```
   100	
   101	or
   102	
   103	```text
   104	D0*C/(3*A^2) = 1.
   105	```
   106	
   107	That is the one-pole ratio reported by the simulation diagnostics.
   108	
   109	---
   110	
   111	## 3. Outgoing prefactor and moment-shape conditions
   112	
   113	The outgoing prefactor is
   114	
   115	```text
   116	P(omega) = D0*N(omega) / D(omega)^2.
   117	```
   118	
   119	Expanding through `O(omega^4)` gives
   120	
   121	```text
   122	P0 = N0/D0,
   123	P2 = (D0*N2 + 2*A*N0)/D0^2,
   124	P4 = (D0^2*N4 + 2*D0*(A*N2 + C*N0) + 3*A^2*N0)/D0^3.
   125	```
   126	
   127	The constant-prefactor branch requires
   128	
   129	```text
   130	P2 = 0,
   131	P4 = 0.
   132	```
   133	
   134	Equivalently,
   135	
   136	```text
   137	N2 = -2*A*N0/D0,
   138	N4 = N0*(A^2 - 2*D0*C)/D0^2.
   139	```
   140	
   141	On the one-pole surface `D0*C = 3*A^2`, this reduces to
   142	
   143	```text
   144	N4 = -5*A^2*N0/D0^2.
   145	```
   146	
   147	This is why the projection-stress diagnostic matters.  Raising `C` or `D0` to
   148	the one-pole surface is not enough.  Scaling the outgoing amplitude to fix `P0`
   149	is also not enough.  The branch must realize the outgoing moment shape through
   150	`N2` and `N4` on the same frozen branch.
   151	
   152	---

   731	### 10.1 Constant-area squish and exact ellipse construction
   732	
   733	After the dynamic-pinning analysis, the next serious question was whether the missing (P_{22}) splitter could appear **induced** rather than already frozen. The key physical correction was to impose a constant-area deformation of the throat cross-section, motivated by the idea that the particle’s mass-supporting inflow should not change under a same-charge spin reorganization. If the throat is squeezed along one transverse axis and elongated along the perpendicular one while preserving area exactly, the natural parametrization is
   734	[
   735	a_\parallel=a,e^{-\xi},
   736	\qquad
   737	a_\perp=a,e^{\xi},
   738	\qquad
   739	A=\pi a_\parallel a_\perp=\pi a^2.
   740	]
   741	So the deformation is not an arbitrary ellipse approximation; it is the exact constant-area one-parameter family.
   742	
   743	In polar form, with principal axis (\phi_0), the boundary is
   744	[
   745	r(\vartheta)
   746	============
   747	
   748	\frac{a}{\sqrt{e^{2\xi}\cos^2(\vartheta-\phi_0)+e^{-2\xi}\sin^2(\vartheta-\phi_0)}}.
   749	]
   750	At small (\xi), this is already an explicit (m=2) distortion. The importance of this construction is that it finally supplies a geometric mechanism for a real in-plane quadrupole without changing the total cross-sectional area.

   753	
   754	Once the exact ellipse is written down, the second-moment tensor of the cross-section immediately produces a traceless in-plane quadrupole.    755	[

   757	=======================

   764	
   765	-\frac{\pi a^4}{2}\sin2\phi,\sinh2\xi.
   766	]
   767	So the constant-area ellipse is not merely “sort of anisotropic.” It is a genuine real (P_{22}) object with amplitude proportional to (\sinh2\xi).
   768

   773

   784	]

The important point is not the particular radial scaling of (V_2), but the fact that an honest (\cos2\phi) splitter emerges from the geometry as soon as the induced deformation is forced to preserve area.

That distinction matters for the lepton program: it means the session found a real route to a two-well same-charge rotor, but not yet a free-particle same-charge spinor theorem.

  1193	## 14. Standing-wave closure and autonomous soliton closure
  1194	
  1195	### 14.1 Stable standing-wave round-trip condition (R_{\rm rt}=1)
  1196	
  1197	The first attempt to kill the scalar phase (\phi_0) was to treat the common support channel as a standing wave on a full internal loop. Writing the scalar round-trip factor as
  1198	[
  1199	R_{\rm rt}=r_0,r_L,e^{2ikL},
  1200	]
  1201	with
  1202	[
  1203	r_0=\rho_0e^{i\delta_0},\qquad
  1204	r_L=\rho_Le^{i\delta_L},
  1205	]
  1206	the full-loop scalar phase is
  1207	[
  1208	\phi_0=\delta_0+\delta_L+2kL.
  1209	]
  1210	If the support wave is a leakage-free trapped standing wave, then after one full scalar round trip it must reproduce itself:
  1211	[
  1212	R_{\rm rt}=1.
  1213	]
  1214	This is the usual cavity/eigenmode condition. It implies
  1215	[
  1216	\rho_0\rho_L=1,
  1217	\qquad
  1218	\phi_0=2\pi N,
  1219	]
  1220	so
  1221	[
  1222	e^{i\phi_0}=1,
  1223	\qquad
  1224	\phi_0\equiv0\pmod{2\pi}.
  1225	]
  1226	
  1227	This was a crucial positive result. It showed that the desired scalar-phase cancellation is not some arbitrary aesthetic choice. It is exactly what one gets if the common support channel is a true leakage-free standing-wave eigenmode.
  1228	
  1229	### 14.2 Why generic steady state is too weak
  1230	
  1231	However, the next thermodynamic test showed that one must be careful not to overstate that result. The handoff suggestion that “thermodynamic steady state” by itself forces
  1232	[

  1234	]
  1235	turned out to be too strong.
  1236	
  1237	The simplest one-cycle amplitude map is
  1238	[
