  1240	\qquad
  1241	\Lambda=\rho e^{i\phi_0},
  1242	]
  1243	where (\Lambda) is the intrinsic round-trip coefficient of the support loop and (D) is a replenishment/pump term over one cycle. The exact fixed point is
  1244	[
  1245	A_*=\frac{D}{1-\Lambda}.
  1246	]
  1247	So a non-decaying steady state with (A_*= \text{const}) does **not** imply
  1248	[
  1249	\Lambda=1
  1250	]
  1251	unless
  1252	[
  1253	D=0.
  1254	]
  1255	
  1256	This is the key loophole the session had to close. A pump-balanced or leakage-balanced steady state can keep the amplitude constant while the intrinsic round-trip coefficient remains different from 1. So “thermodynamic steady state” is not enough by itself to prove the standing-wave closure.
  1257	
  1258	The same distinction appears in the continuous envelope model
  1259	[
  1260	\dot A=\left[\frac{\gamma_{\rm in}-\gamma_{\rm leak}}{2}+i\omega\right]A.
  1261	]
  1262	Steady state only forces
  1263	[
  1264	\gamma_{\rm in}=\gamma_{\rm leak},
  1265	]
  1266	which fixes the modulus. It does not stop the phase from advancing. To make the wave reproduce itself after one loop of duration (T), one still needs the resonance condition
  1267	[
  1268	\omega T=2\pi N.
  1269	]
  1270	
  1271	So the session sharpened the physical alternatives into two genuinely different closures:
  1272	[
  1273	\text{steady amplitude}
  1274	]
  1275	versus
  1276	[
  1277	\text{self-reproducing standing-wave eigenmode}.
  1278	]
  1279	Only the second one kills (\phi_0).

  1281	### 14.3 Difference between driven steady state and autonomous eigenmode
  1282	
  1283	This distinction then became the core conceptual divide in the endgame.
  1284	
  1285	A **driven-dissipative steady state** allows external replenishment or pump balance. In discrete form,
  1286	[
  1287	A_{n+1}=\Lambda A_n + D,
  1288	]

  1290	[
  1291	\dot A=\left[\frac{\gamma_{\rm in}-\gamma_{\rm leak}}{2}+i\omega\right]A.

  1293	Such a state can be perfectly stable in amplitude while carrying a nontrivial phase drift around the loop. It is a fixed point, but not necessarily an eigenmode.
  1294

  1296	[

  1300	\qquad

  1489	
  1490	The remaining gap is now very specific. The current project-side handoffs are explicit that the conservative 1PN/2PN program is solved only within a declared closure hierarchy and still leaves spin couplings, dissipative leakage / radiation reaction, and the fully solved moving-throat PDE unresolved. That means the session did **not** prove, directly from the frozen files alone, that an isolated particle is an autonomous self-reproducing eigenmode. It also did not prove a free-particle, file-derived static (P_{22}) splitter inside the conservative freeze, and it did not derive a genuine non-Abelian (\tau)-exchange transport law. So the half-integer discretizer is now best described as a rigorous **conditional theorem** rather than a finished file-grounded particle theorem.
  1491	
  1492	The honest current status is therefore:
  1493	
  1494	[
  1495	\boxed{
  1496	\text{minimal charged-lepton route: provisionally viable, with one remaining nontrivial closure assumption.}
  1497	}
  1498	]
  1499	
  1500	That assumption is no longer vague. It is precisely the autonomous self-reproducing eigenmode closure of the isolated support channel, together with the central-sign closure on the mixed subbundle. If those two pieces can be derived rather than imposed, the session’s half-integer lock becomes a true theorem of the model. If not, the route remains an elegant but conditional possibility.

   137	## 5. Relationship to spin-1/2 / lepton_work / autonomous-eigenmode closure
   138	
   139	The brief's framing intersects `notes/lepton_work.md` in a non-obvious way that future sessions need to understand.
   140	
   141	`lepton_work.md` §10 documents that the spin-1/2 mechanism rides on an **induced area-preserving `P_{22}` deformation** of the throat mouth, and §14 documents that the same-charge half-integer quantizer is conditional on the isolated particle being an **autonomous self-reproducing standing-wave GNLS soliton**.
   142	
   143	The relationship to Stage 1:
   144	
   145	- The **stationary isotropic branch** (WP1) **is** the autonomous-eigenmode candidate. A Newton solve that converges to a stationary isotropic configuration with stable support modes is implicitly testing whether the parent PDE admits such an autonomous soliton at all. If WP1 has no solution, the §14 closure is unreachable in this model.
   146	- The **grouped P2 tangent** (WP3) **is** the induced-deformation response. The P_{22} mechanism in `lepton_work.md` §10 is a special case of the broader `Y_{2m}` quadrupole linearized response that the brief tests. The coefficients the brief extracts (`D_2, D_4, N_2, N_4`) characterize the response operator whose poles include the resonance the user described ("bumping a particle causes it to resonate").
   147	- **Stage 1 does not directly test spin-1/2.** That's downstream of `lepton_work.md` §14 + §12 (central-sign holonomy) + the recirculation/plumbing closure. Stage 1 only tests whether the foundational autonomous-eigenmode and P2-response structures exist with the right gravity-side coefficients.
   148	
   149	The user explicitly flagged: *"never assume the simple solution works"* in this system. The brief honors that — its targets are coefficients of the **response operator's low-frequency expansion**, not naïve properties of the static configuration. The feedback structure (inflow pressure ↔ wall energy ↔ standing-wave support ↔ brane closure) is *what determines those coefficients* on the realized branch. A successful Stage 1 means the feedback closes self-consistently and produces the right numbers; a failure tells you which sector of the feedback didn't close.
   150	
   185	## 8. Prerequisites
   186	
   187	These must be true before Stage 1 work begins:
   188	
   189	1. **Parent operator frozen.** `research/pde_audit/simulation/NONLINEAR_PROTOCOL_V2.md` records that `S_eta`/`S_Sigma` promotion and the full coupled physical residual equations are not yet frozen. The active red-team is part of what will land them.
   190	2. **PDE-ledger red-team complete.** Currently 60/253 stages verified (see [[project-moving-throat-verification]] in auto-memory). Stage 1 work should not start until the red-team's first end-to-end pass is done; the user has also planned a second cross-check pass before downstream computational work (see [[project-full-second-pass]]).
   191	3. **A pre-registration document.** Before any compute is spent, freeze: which branch, which boundary protocol, which gauge convention, which outgoing-port convention, which observable is primary. Per brief §3.4 — once written, do not edit after seeing data.
   192	
   195	## 9. What success means in the analog-framework frame
   196	
   197	Stage 1 success **is not** "evidence the model describes physical reality." (User has not made and does not intend to make that claim — see [[project-analog-framework-goal]].)
   198	
   199	Stage 1 success **is** "the analog framework is self-consistent and operationally demonstrable: one set of equations, reduced two ways, returning the right coefficients in both reductions, with a validated noise floor." That delivers the project's stated deliverable — a working mathematical bridge between EM and gravity formalisms — at the strongest level a single solo-researcher-plus-AI program can deliver.
   200	
   201	A trustworthy Stage 1 miss is also a valid outcome. It says: the analog as currently written does not close all the way through; here is which coefficient does not match; here is the validated error budget around that statement. That is publishable, citable, and useful — particularly because the prior 4d_1pn_sim attempt could not produce a trustworthy verdict either direction.
   202	
   203	Stage 2 (novel-prediction extraction) is the test of whether the analog also *says something new and right*. Stage 1 is the gate to running Stage 2 honestly.

     2	
     3	## Executive verdict
     4	
     5	This audit **accepts the architectural patch** from a capped throat to an open finite-radius conduit:
     6	
     7	\[
     8	R(L)>0,
     9	\]
    10	
    11	with the bottom of the throat opening into unconfined four-spatial-dimensional bulk. A hard cap,
    12	
    13	\[
    14	R(L)=0,
    15	\]
    16	
    17	is incompatible with a nonzero baseline/DC superfluid throughput, because the exit area vanishes and a fixed flux would require a divergent flux density.
    18	
    19	The audit gives a split result for the D/N support ladder:
    20	
    21	\[
    22	\textbf{D/N survives only if the support variable is the free-end flow/displacement variable.}
    23	\]
    24	
    25	A sudden expansion into a large bulk reservoir is a **low-impedance open end**. For a pressure-like or potential-like scalar, that open end reflects with phase \(\pi\),
    26	
    27	\[
    28	R_p\to -1,
    29	\]
    30	
    31	which is Dirichlet-like. For the dual flow/displacement variable, the reflected amplitude has the opposite sign,
    32	
    33	\[
    34	R_q=-R_p\to +1,
    35	\]
    36	
    37	which is Neumann-like:
    38	
    39	\[
    40	\frac{q_w(L)}{q(L)}\to0.
    41	\]
    42	
    43	So the organ-pipe patch is viable, but the Volume 2 wording must be precise:
    44	
    45	> The open throat dynamically produces the D/N ladder for the **flow/displacement support coordinate**, not for a generic pressure-like scalar field.
    46

    54	S_\psi^{(2)}

   253	
   254	For a tube mode near the exit,
   255	
   256	\[
   257	f(w)
   258	=
   259	e^{ik(w-L)}
   260	+

   262	\]
   263

   265

   268	=
   269	ik\frac{1-R}{1+R}.
   270	\]
   271	
   272	### Pressure/potential-like scalar
   273	
   274	Using
   275	
   276	\[
   277	R_p=\frac{\epsilon-1}{\epsilon+1},
   278	\]

   280	the derivative ratio becomes
   281	
   282	\[
   283	\frac{p_w}{p}
   284	=
   285	\frac{ik}{\epsilon}.
   286	\]
   287	
   288	As \(\epsilon\to0\),
   289	
   290	\[
   291	p(L)=1+R_p\to0.
   292	\]
   293	
   294	So the open end is Dirichlet-like for \(p\):
   295

   297	p(L)\simeq0.
   298	\]
   299

   304	\]
   305

   309	
   310	For the dual support variable,
   311	
   312	\[
   313	R_q=\frac{1-\epsilon}{1+\epsilon},
   314	\]
   315	
   316	and
   317	
   318	\[
   319	\frac{q_w}{q}
   320	=
   321	ik\epsilon.

   325

   327	\frac{q_w(L)}{q(L)}\to0,
   328	\]
   329

   331	
   332	\[
   333	q_w(L)\simeq0.
   334	\]
   335	
   336	With the mouth condition
   337	
   338	\[
   339	q(0)=0,
   340	\]

   343

   345	q_j(w)=A\sin(k_j w),
   346	\]
   347

   349	q_j'(L)=0,
   350	\]

   356	\]

   359

   363	}
   364	\]
   365	
   366	So the D/N support ladder is validated by the open-junction mechanism only after the support coordinate is identified as the free-end flow/displacement variable, or an equivalent conjugate variable.

   370	## 4. DC leakage and the zero-mode
   438	| Strong AC reflection from sudden expansion | **Pass** | \(\mathcal T_E=4\epsilon/(1+\epsilon)^2=O(\epsilon)\) for \(\epsilon\ll1\). |
   439	| Neumann reflection for generic scalar \(\psi\) | **Fail** | Pressure/potential-like scalar has \(R_p\to-1\), Dirichlet-like. |
   440	| Neumann reflection for flow/displacement support variable | **Pass** | Dual variable has \(R_q\to+1\), \(q_w/q=ik\epsilon\to0\). |
   441	| D/N ladder | **Conditional pass** | Valid if the finite-throat support field is the free-end flow/displacement coordinate or an impedance-transformed equivalent. |

   446	
   447	Replace the old cap language with:
   448

The conjugate pressure/potential variable sees the usual open-end Dirichlet-like phase, while the support displacement/flow coordinate sees a Neumann-like condition. The baseline/DC superfluid current exits through the same open junction and is tracked by the existing leakage/current bookkeeping.
   450	
   451	This preserves both requirements:
   467	If the program insists that the D/N field \(\psi\) is pressure-like or potential-like, then a sudden expansion does **not** generate the required Neumann condition.
   468	
   469	To recover Neumann for that variable, one needs an effective high-impedance input:
   470	
   471	\[
   472	\frac{Z_L}{Z_t}\gg1.
   473	\]
   474	
   475	That requires one of the following:
   476	
   477	1. a narrow high-impedance neck,
   478	2. a quarter-wave impedance transformer,
   479	3. a side-branch/stub resonator whose input impedance is high at the support frequencies,
   480	4. or a variable redefinition in which the D/N support coordinate is the dual flow/displacement variable.
   481	
   482	The simplest patch is option 4.

   491

   494	\]
   495	
   496	not
   497

    33	## What the paper claims
    34	
    35	Stage 001 is the foundational geometry-lift stage. It replaces the finite-dimensional collective variables `a(t), L(t)` by a distributed throat shape field `Σ(X,t)=r-R(Ω,w,t)` (eq:app-stage001-sigma), recovering `a,L` as lowest moments, and sets up the first linearized matter/gauge/geometry system. Its `\stagefield{Output}` (tex:223) verbatim: *"The stage outputs the shape-field closure \eqref{eq:app-stage001-sigma}, the confinement variation \eqref{eq:app-stage001-delta-v}, the harmonic split \eqref{eq:app-stage001-harmonic-expansion}, the modal wall PDE \eqref{eq:app-stage001-modal-wall-pde}, and the response-operator target \eqref{eq:app-stage001-response-operator}. These are the definitions without which later grouped response coefficients have no PDE-side interpretation."* The card's `\stagefield{Verification}` (tex:11) narrows what the audits should check to three load-bearing identities: *"the monopole/P2 harmonic bookkeeping, the confinement chain-rule sign, and the densitized-versus-weighted wall-action convention."* The `\stagefield{Checks}` checklist (tex:225-230) lists: the moment relation `q_{00}=2√π δa`, the sign of `δV_conf` from `δΣ=-η`, harmonic-orthogonality selection (no l=0↔l=2 mixing), and the ontology check (keep `A_w,J^w,F_{μw}` alive). The notes add the boxed linearized Maxwell law `∂_M(Z(w)δF^{MN})+(1/ξ)∂^N(∂·δA)=μ0 δJ^N` (§8) and the eigenvalue specialization `−Δ_{S²}Y_{lm}=l(l+1)Y_{lm}` driving the modal split (§5). It is a checkpoint stage and is `is_status_only_candidate: False`, so both engines are required.
    36	
    37	## What the script claims to verify
    38	
    39	The SymPy script (docstring lines 8-22) and the assertions verify: (I) normalized real-harmonic bookkeeping — `Y00=1/(2√π)`, unit norms, zero averages for the five real P2 modes, orthogonality `cross(Y00,Y20)=0`, the mouth-average extraction `q00=2√π δa`, and the spherical-Laplacian eigenvalue `−Δ_{S²}=l(l+1)` (i.e. `6` for l=2); (II) the confinement chain-rule sign `δV_conf=−(V'_wall(Σ0/ℓc)/ℓc)η` via a genuine ε-variation; (III) the modal wall Euler–Lagrange equation in both the densitized and weighted-surface conventions, the `K_l` restoring-shift specialization at l=0,2, and the sourced RHS; (IV) a representative two-component (x,w) localized-Maxwell linearization with the `Z(w)` weight, gauge-fixing term, and source current. The Mathematica `.wl` mirrors the same checks and adds an independent `SphericalHarmonicY`-based eigenvalue confirmation (I.3b) and uses `VariationalD` for the Maxwell sector. Every check is an `expect_zero`/`expectZero` against a hand-written target; the saved outputs show all residuals `= 0` and all `PASS`.

    81	## Findings
    82	
    83	None.
    84	
    85	### Adversarial attacks attempted (all failed to break the scripts)
    86	
    87	1. **Sign of δV_conf.** Verified by hand: `d/dε Vwall((Σ0−εη)/ℓc)|_{ε=0} = −(η/ℓc)V'_wall(Σ0/ℓc)`, and the script's target `−η·∂_{Σ0}Vwall(Σ0/ℓc) = −(η/ℓc)V'_wall`. Both carry the 1/ℓc and the minus sign. Matches boxed eq:app-stage001-delta-v (tex:91) and notes §3. No sign flip.
    88	2. **Euler–Lagrange sign convention (Section III).** SymPy `euler_equations` returns `∂L/∂q − Σ_i d/dx_i(∂L/∂q_{x_i}) = 0`. With `ldens = ½μq_t²−½T_w q_w²−½k_l q²` this gives `−μq_tt + d/dw(T_w q_w) − k_l q`, exactly `target_dens` (py:166). Matches modal wall PDE. The weighted form correctly produces the `d/dw(g·T_w q_w)` term that, on division by g, yields the extra first-derivative term the paper (tex:149) and notes (§5) describe.
    89	3. **Maxwell EL signs (Section IV).** Hand-derived both components. `el_Ax = d/dw(Z F_wx) + d/dx(divA)/ξ − μ0 J_x` and `el_Aw = −d/dx(Z F_wx) + d/dw(divA)/ξ − μ0 J_w`; both equal the script targets (py:225-226). The opposite-sign relation between SymPy's manual EL operator and Mathematica's `VariationalD` is correctly handled by the leading `−` on `VariationalD` (wl:208-209, comment wl:206-207).
    90	4. **Eigenvalue constant "6".** `l(l+1)` at l=2 is 6; the script proves this is not a magic literal both by computing `−Δ_{S²}Y_{2m}=6Y_{2m}` directly (A5/B3) and independently via `SphericalHarmonicY` (B4), and by the `K_l(2)=K_η+6T_Ω` specialization (A9).
    91	5. **q00=2√π δa.** `(1/4π)∫η dΩ = q00·(1/4π)·2√π = q00/(2√π)`, so δa=q00/(2√π) ⇒ q00=2√π δa. Matches tex:127 and notes §4. The P2 terms drop out because their averages vanish (A1) — so the script's inclusion of q20,q21c,q22c in `eta` (py:110) genuinely tests that they don't contaminate the monopole average; this is non-trivial, not scaffolding.
    92	6. **Symbol assumptions.** SymPy: `nonzero=True` on Σ0/η/ℓc/eps (Section II) is harmless and does not over-strengthen any simplify; `0<θ<π` is implicit via the integration domain; Mathematica uses `0<θ<π`, `ℓc>0`, `ξ>0`, `μ0>0`. None of these assumptions are strong enough to force a false `==0` (the targets are subtracted, so an over-aggressive simplify would still need the algebra to actually cancel). No `symbol_assumption_error`.

    94	## Findings
    95	
    96	### F1 — paper_misalignment
    97	
    98	**Severity:** medium
    99	**Subtype:** target_mismatch (sign convention on source coupling)
   100	**Files:**
   101	- `/var/projects/toy_physics/research/pde_ledger/scripts/moving_throat_pde_stage001_geometry_lift_sympy_audit.py:188-192`
   102	- `/var/projects/toy_physics/research/pde_ledger/mathematica/moving_throat_pde_stage001_geometry_lift_mathematica_audit.wl:184-192`
   103	- paper side: `/var/projects/toy_physics/research/pde_ledger/paper/stages/stage_001.tex:158-162` (boxed eq:app-stage001-modal-wall-pde)
   104	- notes side: `/var/projects/toy_physics/research/pde_ledger/notes/stages/moving_throat_pde_stage001_geometry_lift.md:358-361`
   105	
   106	**What's wrong:**
   107	
   108	Paper boxed eq:app-stage001-modal-wall-pde (`stage_001.tex:156-163`):
   109	
   110	```
   111	mu_eta partial_t^2 q_{lm} - partial_w(T_w partial_w q_{lm}) + [K_eta + l(l+1) T_Omega] q_{lm}
   112	    = S_{lm}^{(psi,A)} + f_{lm}^{ext}
   113	```
   114	
   115	Notes (lines 358-361) match: `... = S_{lm}^{(psi,A)} + f_{lm}^{ext}`. Both state the source enters the RHS with a **positive** sign.
   116	
   117	SymPy script `sympy_audit.py:188-192`:
   118	
   119	```python
   120	source_total = S_lm(t, w) + f_ext(t, w)
   121	ldens_forced = ldens - q(t, w) * source_total
   122	el_forced = euler_equations(ldens_forced, q(t, w), [t, w])[0]
   123	target_forced = target_dens - source_total
   124	expect_zero("sourced densitized Euler-Lagrange equation", el_forced.lhs - target_forced)
   125	```
   126	
   127	SymPy's `euler_equations` returns `Eq(∂L/∂q − Σ_i d/dx_i ∂L/∂(∂_{x_i} q), 0)`. With `ldens_forced = ldens − q · source_total`, `∂L/∂q` gains an extra `−source_total`, so `el_forced.lhs = target_dens − source_total = 0`, i.e.,
   128	
   129	```
   130	mu_eta partial_t^2 q − partial_w(T_w partial_w q) + K_l q = −(S_lm + f_ext).
   131	```
   132	
   133	That is the **negative** of the paper's boxed RHS. The Mathematica script (`mathematica_audit.wl:187-192`) does the identical thing: `ldensForced = ldens − qField*sourceTotal` and asserts the same sign-flipped form. The summary line in both scripts ("the sourced modal-wall RHS forcing S_lm^(psi,A) + f_lm^ext") explicitly claims to verify the paper's positive-RHS form, but the assertion exercises the opposite sign.
   134	
   135	**Why this matters:**
   136	
   137	The script silently certifies a convention opposite to the one the paper publishes. Downstream stages quoting eq:app-stage001-modal-wall-pde will get the wrong sign on the source if they trust the script's sign convention rather than the paper's. Stage 003 in particular uses this modal-wall PDE form as the wall-BdG coupling and depends on the correct sign for the back-reaction direction. For a checkpoint stage, this is a real defect.
   138	
   139	**Required change:**
   140	
   141	Script-side, single-sign flip: the Lagrangian coupling term should be `+q · source` (so that `∂L/∂q` produces `+source`, leaving `+source` on the equation RHS), not `−q · source`.
   142	
   143	- SymPy (`sympy_audit.py:189`): change `ldens_forced = ldens - q(t, w) * source_total` → `ldens_forced = ldens + q(t, w) * source_total`. Update line 191 `target_forced = target_dens - source_total` → `target_forced = target_dens + source_total`.
   144	- Mathematica (`mathematica_audit.wl:188`): change `ldensForced = ldens - qField*sourceTotal` → `ldensForced = ldens + qField*sourceTotal`. Update line 191 `targetForced = targetDens - sourceTotal` → `targetForced = targetDens + sourceTotal`.
   145	
   146	After this fix, the equation verified will be `mu q_tt − ∂_w(T_w q_w) + K_l q = +(S_lm + f_ext)`, matching the paper.
   147	
   148	**Verification:**
   149	
   150	Re-run the script; output line "sourced densitized Euler-Lagrange equation = 0" should still print `0` (the identity remains true under consistently-flipped signs on both sides). The substantive change is in the Lagrangian → equation correspondence the assertion exercises. Manual inspection: the new `ldens_forced` line should show `+ q(t,w) * source_total` and the new `target_forced` line should show `+ source_total`.
   151	
   152	### F2 — paper_misalignment
   153	
   154	**Severity:** low (likely metric-signature convention question, not a substantive sign error in the math)
   155	**Subtype:** target_mismatch (gauge-term sign in linearized Maxwell — pending user resolution on metric signature)
   156	**Files:**
   157	- `/var/projects/toy_physics/research/pde_ledger/paper/stages/stage_001.tex:192-198` (boxed eq:app-stage001-linear-maxwell)
   158	- `/var/projects/toy_physics/research/pde_ledger/scripts/moving_throat_pde_stage001_geometry_lift_sympy_audit.py:209-229`
   159	- `/var/projects/toy_physics/research/pde_ledger/mathematica/moving_throat_pde_stage001_geometry_lift_mathematica_audit.wl:194-213`
   160	
   161	**What's wrong:**
   162	
   163	Paper boxed eq:app-stage001-linear-maxwell reads
   164	```
   165	partial_M(Z(w) delta F^{MN}) + (1/xi) partial^N(partial . delta A) = mu_0 delta J^N,
   166	```
   167	i.e., the gauge-fix term has a `+(1/xi) partial^N` sign. The raised-index `partial^N` makes the sign of the term as written in `partial_N` coordinates dependent on metric signature.
   168	
   169	SymPy script defines (lines 209-213):
   170	```python
   171	lmax = (
   172	    sp.Rational(1, 2) * Zloc(w) * Fwx**2
   173	    - sp.Rational(1, 2) * divA**2 / gauge_xi
   174	    + mu0 * (Jx(x, w) * Ax(x, w) + Jw(x, w) * Aw(x, w))
   175	)
   176	```
   177	and asserts (line 228) `el_Ax - target_Ax = 0` with
   178	```python
   179	target_Ax = sp.diff(Zloc(w) * Fwx, w) - sp.diff(divA, x) / gauge_xi - mu0 * Jx(x, w)
   180	```
   181	Setting this to zero gives `partial_w(Z F_wx) - partial_x(divA)/xi = mu_0 J_x`.
   182	
   183	Reading the paper's boxed equation under a mostly-plus metric (`partial^x = partial_x` for spatial indices): `partial_w(Z F^{wx}) + partial_x(divA)/xi = mu_0 J_x`. **The gauge-fix term has opposite sign in script vs paper-mostly-plus.**
   184	
   185	If the parent theory uses a `(+,−,−,−,−)` mostly-minus signature, then `partial^x = −partial_x` and the paper's `+(1/xi) partial^N(...)` rewrites as `−(1/xi) partial_x(...)` for spatial N, which would match the script. The paper card does not state the metric signature, and the audit prompt restricts the auditor's reading to this unit's files.
   186	
   187	**Why this matters:**
   188	
   189	If the signature is mostly-plus, the script verifies a Maxwell equation with a sign-flipped gauge term — internally consistent against its own Lagrangian but not the paper's published form. If mostly-minus, no defect. Either way, the metric convention is load-bearing for sign comparisons and should be made explicit either in the paper card (one-line statement of signature) or in the script docstring.
   190	
   191	**Required change:**
   192	
   193	Routes to user — see directive `## Resolve before fix_loop` block. The auditor cannot determine the metric signature from the audit reading list. Codex must not silently flip the sign in either direction.
   194	
   195	**Verification:**
   196

     2	
     3	## Purpose
     4	
     5	This stage consolidates the isotropic moving-throat full-bundle target into a finite pass/fail packet for an actual branch extraction.
     6	
     7	Earlier Volume 2 stages verified the ingredients separately:
     8	
     9	- the conservative grouped response bridge,
    10	- the outgoing `l=2` fingerprint,
    11	- the 2.5PN / 4PN normalization interface,

    14	- and the quotient / similarity-orbit structure.

   236	The incidence matrix printed by the script is a dependency ledger, not a fit instruction. It shows which frozen branch data are used by which residual.
   237	
   238	The key interpretation is:
   239	
   240	- dependencies from branch data to residuals are allowed;
   241	- dependencies from residuals or target decisions back to branch data are forbidden.
   242

   245	## 4. Why the no-refit rule is mandatory
   246	
   247	The script computes the Jacobian of the five residuals with respect to the post-hoc knob set
   248	
   249	\[
   250	(K,N_2,N_4,N_0,\Theta_{\rm tail}).
   251	\]
   252	
   253	It finds
   254	
   255	\[
   256	\det
   257	\frac{\partial(R_{\rm pole},R_{P2},R_{P4},R_{\rm norm},R_{\rm tail})}
   258	{\partial(K,N_2,N_4,N_0,\Theta_{\rm tail})}
   259	=
   260	\frac{
   261	\mathcal S_{\rm port}\widehat m_0^{\,2}(B_4+Z_4)
   262	}{
   263	D_0^3
   264	}
   265	\left(\frac{c}{c_s}\right)^3.
   266	\]
   267	
   268	Equivalently, as printed in the script’s native sign convention,
   269	
   270	\[
   271	-\frac{
   272	\mathcal S_{\rm port}c^3\widehat m_0^{\,2}(B_4+Z_4)
   273	}{
   274	c_s^3(B_0-K+Z_0)^3
   275	}.
   276	\]
   277	
   278	Under generic nonzero/stable conditions,
   279	
   280	\[
   281	D_0\neq0,
   282	\qquad
   283	B_4+Z_4\neq0,
   284	\qquad
   285	\widehat m_0\mathcal S_{\rm port}\neq0,
   286	\qquad
   287	c/c_s\neq0,
   288	\]
   289	
   290	this determinant is nonzero.
   291	
   292	Therefore, if post-hoc fitting were allowed, five algebraic knobs could generically tune five residuals. That is the point of this stage: the algebra is powerful enough that target comparison is not trustworthy without a freeze certificate.
   293

   297

   299

   301

   303	parent action and current bookkeeping
   304	gauge-fixing convention
   305	wall/throat action or effective interface action
   306	open-exit impedance boundary protocol
   307	projection/source-map convention
   308	support profile family and number of modes/ports
   309	stability acceptance gates
   310	coefficient extraction formulas
   311	```
   312	
   313	Only after these are frozen may the branch evaluate:
   314	
   315	```text
   316	one-pole residual
   317	constant-prefactor residuals
   318	universal quadrupole normalization
   319	tail-transport scalar
   320	weak-axisymmetric prefactor slope Xi_1
   321	```
   322	
   323	Forbidden after target evaluation:
   324	
   325	```text
   326	changing support-cardinality
   327	changing boundary condition class
   328	changing gauge convention
   329	changing port/source normalization convention
   330	dropping dark or unstable branches only after target miss unless this was predeclared

    17

    19	tail transport speed, or the Maxwell localization speed depends on the
    20	superfluid density, then density is a load-bearing branch variable rather than
    21	a hidden constant.
    22	
    23	---
    24	
    25	## 1. What is already present
    26	
    27	The project has not completely ignored the superfluid equation of state.
    28	Several notes carry a frozen stiff-polytropic closure of the schematic form
    29	
    30	```text
    31	P(rho) = K_EOS rho^n
    32	h(rho) = n K_EOS rho^(n-1)/(n-1)
    33	c_s^2(rho) = (1/m) dP/drho.
    34	```
    35	
    36	For the commonly carried `n = 5` branch this gives
    37	
    38	```text
    39	c_s^2(rho) = (5 K_EOS/m) rho^4.
    40	```
    41	
    42	The notes also contain background-density formulas in reduced Thomas-Fermi or
    43	stationary-branch settings, and some 2PN-side material uses normalized
    44	sound-speed functions such as `C_s(u)=c_s^2(u)/c_s0^2`.
    45	
    46	So the right statement is not:
    47	
    48	```text
    49	There is no EOS anywhere in the project.
    50	```
    51	
    52	The right statement is:
    53	
    54	```text
    55	The EOS appears as a reduced or frozen constitutive ingredient, but it is not
    56	yet closed into the audited moving-throat branch exporter.
    57	```
    58	
    59	---
    60

    62	
    63	The current audit and simulation packets mostly treat
    64	
    65	```text
    66	rho0, c_s, c, K_EOS, Z(w), W(w)
    67	```
    68	
    69	as symbolic constants, fixture inputs, normalization choices, or frozen branch
    70	data.  That is acceptable for checking conditional algebra, but it is not a
    71	completed physical PDE.
    72

    74	
    75	1. The superfluid density field:
    76	
    77	   ```text

    79	   ```
    80

    84

    87	   ```
    88

    90

    93	   ```
    94

    96

   143	to match observed physics.

   151	  equation, not just a scalar normalization condition.

   157	
   158	This gives a plausible reason why the reduced algebra can be clean while the

   377	### 4.2 Poisson hook
   378	
   379	With the Helmholtz decomposition
   380	\[
   381	\mathbf v_{\rm brane}=\nabla_3\varphi+\mathbf v_T,\qquad \nabla_3\cdot \mathbf v_T=0,
   382	\]
   383	one obtains the exact longitudinal identity
   384	\[
   385	\boxed{
   386	\rho_{\rm brane}\,\nabla_3^2\varphi
   387	=
   388	S_{\rm leak}
   389	-\partial_t\rho_{\rm brane}
   390	-(\nabla_3\rho_{\rm brane})\cdot(\nabla_3\varphi+\mathbf v_T).
   391	}
   392	\]
   393	
   394	In the quasi-static longitudinal regime this reduces to a Poisson equation on the brane.
   395	
   396	### 4.3 Zero-mode Maxwell reduction
   397	
   398	Under the controlled far-field zero-mode assumptions
   399	\[
   400	A_w\approx 0,\qquad
   401	\partial_w A_\mu\approx 0,\qquad
   402	J^w\approx 0,\qquad
   403	F_{\mu w}\approx 0,
   404	\]
   405	integration over \(w\) gives an effective brane Maxwell sector
   406	\[
   407	\partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu}=\mu_0^{\rm eff}J_{\rm eff}^\nu,
   408	\qquad
   409	\mu_0^{\rm eff}=\frac{\mu_0}{Z_{\rm int}}.
   410	\]
   411	
   412	This is a **controlled reduction**, not a denial of the mixed-core structure.

   546

   574	\]
   575	with frequencies

   581	}

   592	}
   593	\]
   594

It is not automatically circular: Stage 001 introduces `S_eta^(2)` as a new ansatz with fixed constitutive functions, not coefficients refit stage-by-stage ([moving_throat_pde_stage001_geometry_lift.md](/var/projects/toy_physics/research/pde_ledger/notes/stages/moving_throat_pde_stage001_geometry_lift.md:194), [line 214](/var/projects/toy_physics/research/pde_ledger/notes/stages/moving_throat_pde_stage001_geometry_lift.md:214)); V2-16 explicitly forbids residuals feeding back into branch data and notes five knobs could otherwise tune five residuals ([stage_v2_16_branch_freeze_no_refit_derivation.md](/var/projects/toy_physics/research/pde_audit/notes/stage_v2_16_branch_freeze_no_refit_derivation.md:236), [line 247](/var/projects/toy_physics/research/pde_audit/notes/stage_v2_16_branch_freeze_no_refit_derivation.md:247)). The V2-23 reduced branch was target-blind, open/stable, and failed rather than being rescued ([stage_v2_23_minimal_branch_solver_derivation.md](/var/projects/toy_physics/research/pde_audit/notes/stage_v2_23_minimal_branch_solver_derivation.md:24), [line 320](/var/projects/toy_physics/research/pde_audit/notes/stage_v2_23_minimal_branch_solver_derivation.md:320)). So a B-run can produce a meaningful “yes/no” for the effective branch, provided the pre-registration names it that way.

Path A is not derivable from the existing ledger as a completed object. Existing material gives a quadratic effective wall ansatz; red-team provenance classifies `mu_eta`, `T_w`, `T_Omega`, and `K_eta` as `free_choice` / posited constitutive functions, not derived or externally anchored ([fit_stage001...mu_eta.yaml](/var/projects/toy_physics/research/pde_ledger/redteam_adversarial/provenance/_synthesis/batch_01/fit_stage001_wall_action_constitutive_coefficients__mu_eta.yaml:11), [fit_stage001...k_eta.yaml](/var/projects/toy_physics/research/pde_ledger/redteam_adversarial/provenance/_synthesis/batch_01/fit_stage001_wall_action_constitutive_coefficients__k_eta.yaml:19)). A promoted nonlinear `S_Sigma[R]` would therefore be a fresh parent-level posit unless independently derived. That reopens layer-2-style audit for the throat sector: action, variation, boundary terms, coupled residuals, Jacobian/manufactured tests, stability gates, and no-refit provenance.

3. Non-rescue implications: B-first is clean only if the pre-registration says, in advance, “this is the effective-closure branch.” A B miss then falsifies that branch. It cannot be followed by “we now promote `S_Sigma` and count that as the same Stage-1 attempt.” A later A test is allowed only as a new, separately pre-registered model/branch with its own audit trail. ACTUAL_BRANCH_PROTOCOL’s row is exactly this fork: declare strict `S_Sigma` promotion or explicitly label effective closure ([ACTUAL_BRANCH_PROTOCOL_V1.md](/var/projects/toy_physics/research/pde_audit/simulation/ACTUAL_BRANCH_PROTOCOL_V1.md:23)).

4. Conceptual flag check: Path B does **not** foreclose the Stage-1 gravity-side coefficient test. The execution plan explicitly says 2D Stage 1 captures the P2 response but not the full spin-1/2 chain ([branch_realization_execution_plan.md](/var/projects/toy_physics/docs/branch_realization_execution_plan.md:39)). `lepton_work.md` makes the half-integer quantizer conditional on an autonomous self-reproducing standing-wave GNLS soliton, and says that step is not yet file-grounded ([lepton_work.md](/var/projects/toy_physics/notes/lepton_work.md:1424), [line 1444](/var/projects/toy_physics/notes/lepton_work.md:1444)). So B is safe for Stage 1 if scoped as “effective branch realization.” Escalate to the user only if “permanent effective closure” is intended as a program-wide abandonment of any later autonomous-field/eigenmode completion while still preserving the lepton/spin physical claim.

5. Recommendation: do **B first**, but rename it precisely: “Stage-1 effective-closure branch-realization test.” Freeze `parent_action_status = effective_closure`, support coordinate, D/N/open-impedance convention, wall constitutive packet, material inputs, port list, extraction formulas, and primary observables before compute. Treat the result as a verdict on that branch only. Then run A later as a separate parent-completion program if B is informative enough or if the project needs strict physical export. This ordering is not a non-rescue violation unless A is tuned or advertised as a continuation of the same failed pre-registration.
